Pékin prépare un contrôle inédit sur l’exportation de ses modèles d’IA
items.description: Aujourd’hui, vendredi 16 octobre, les ministères chinois du Commerce et des Sciences et Technologies ont soumis à consultation un projet de révision du catalogue des technologies dont l’exportation est interdite ou soumise à autorisation projet de révision du Catalogue des technologies dont l’exportation est interdite ou restreinte , mis en consultation publique le 16 octobre 2026.'> 1 . Quarante technologies ont été ajoutées à cette liste, qui impose une autorisation pour certains transferts de savoir-faire et en interdit d'autres. Vingt-trois d'entre elles relèvent du domaine de l’intelligence artificielle. Cette consultation se poursuit jusqu’au 15 novembre, mais une obligation d’enregistrement provisoire est d’ores et déjà en vigueur. Le texte vise les poids et le code source des grands modèles au-delà d’un seuil de performance Bloomberg il serait fixé à 2 000 milliards de paramètres ou à une place parmi les dix premiers modèles mondiaux sur des tests de performance et de sécurité.'> 2 , ainsi que les agents intelligents, les architectures de clusters de calcul et les méthodes de conception de puces gravées en 14 nanomètres ou moins. Quatorze technologies sont strictement interdites, dont la génération de code malveillant, tandis que les autres sont soumises à autorisation. Cette mesure annonce-t-elle la fin des grands modèles open source chinois ? En soumettant à autorisation les poids des modèles les plus puissants, le texte vise précisément la catégorie dans laquelle les laboratoires chinois publient aujourd’hui en accès libre, de DeepSeek à Qwen en passant par GLM et Kimi. Un modèle déjà diffusé resterait hors champ, mais les suivants pourraient être soumis à autorisation, voire interdits. Comme le souligne la chercheuse Zilan Qian, ce même document annonce pourtant un mécanisme destiné à faciliter la diffusion de code open source. MofCom said they will have a near auto licensing regime for open-source AI that allows more rapid release it seems ? "To support the development of an open-source AI innovation ecosystem, automatic licensing and other facilitation measures will apply to technology exports… https://t.co/rxP9lyzq5Z pic.twitter.com/qlh0bt2vaz — Zilan Qian (@ZilanQian) October 16, 2026 Les ministères ont en effet annoncé des « mesures de facilitation », dont l’octroi automatique d’autorisations, « afin de soutenir la construction d’un écosystème d’innovation en open source dans le domaine de l’intelligence artificielle » 商务部新闻发言人就修订《中国禁止出口限制出口技术目录》答记者问 , 16 octobre 2026.'> 3 . En prolongeant la doctrine « IA+ » de Xi Jinping, ces mesures s’accompagneraient de la construction et de l’exploitation de centres de données à l’étranger par des entreprises chinoises, de la production de puces hors de Chine, de la recherche conjointe mobilisant des ressources étrangères, ainsi que de la participation à l’élaboration de normes internationales. En réalité, Pékin pourrait être en train de se doter d’un pouvoir discrétionnaire. L’ouverture, qui permet de diffuser les normes chinoises et d’éroder l’avance commerciale des entreprises technologiques américaines, reste la stratégie privilégiée du Parti. Face à l’attention internationale suscitée par cette annonce, Pékin a tenu à affirmer que cette mesure est une politique de sûreté, et non une arme commerciale. Les ministères justifient les interdictions par le fait que les technologies de génération et de modification autonomes de code malveillant « peuvent servir à attaquer les infrastructures d’information critiques, l’industrie de défense ou les systèmes gouvernementaux essentiels, ou à contourner les dispositifs de sécurité nationale ». Ils insistent sur le caractère ordinaire de cette révision, qui « ne vise aucun pays, région ou entité en particulier », et sur le fait que « la position politique n’a pas changé ». Selon la chercheuse Kristy Loke, il faut donc y voir moins un levier de négociation qu’un régime de gestion des risques liés à l’intelligence artificielle, annoncé dans le dernier plan quinquennal publication sur X , 16 octobre 2026.'> 4 . Comme le relève le journaliste spécialiste de la Chine Corbin Duncan, un non-dit semble affleurer dans cette séquence. Le projet vise à interdire l’exportation des technologies d’intelligence artificielle capables de « générer et de modifier de manière autonome du code malveillant », ainsi qu'à restreindre celles qui servent à découvrir des failles de sécurité. Or, une interdiction par capacité suppose qu’on puisse l’isoler, alors qu’elle découle de l’intelligence générale du modèle : « Si l’intelligence se généralise, comment les laboratoires chinois pourront-ils distinguer un modèle performant d’un modèle doté des capacités visées par les restrictions ? » publication sur X , 16 octobre 2026.'> 5 L’article Pékin prépare un contrôle inédit sur l’exportation de ses modèles d’IA est apparu en premier sur Le Grand Continent .

items.title: Father escapes jail after 3-yr-old son falls to death in Cyprus hotel
items.description: A Cyprus court on Friday ordered a British father to pay a fine but spared him prison after he pleaded guilty to causing the death of his three-year-old son, who fell from a hotel window. Joshua Foster’s parents and other relatives were in court for the sentencing, with some weeping and embracing him after the decision was announced, according to Cypriot state media. The incident occurred in the holiday town of Paphos in July on the family’s first day on vacation. The court heard that Foster and other family members had spent time around the hotel pool before returning to their rooms to prepare for dinner. He then left the room with his son and the child’s grandfather. While they waited for the lift, he placed the child on a windowsill so that he could see a nearby water park, not realising that the window was open. The boy fell approximately 10 metres (33 feet) from the fourth floor. Despite efforts to resuscitate him, the child was pronounced dead at the local hospital. In its decision, the Paphos District Court described the incident as a “momentary error” rather than a deliberate act. Foster’s lawyer had asked the court to consider his guilty plea to the charge of causing death through a reckless, rash or dangerous act, as well as his clean criminal record and immeasurable personal loss. Speaking to reporters after the decision, defender Alexandros Alexandrou said that the “court accepted this was a momentary mistake, not conscious negligence”, arguing the case never should have gone to court. “This was an unfortunate incident. Any sentence cannot bring justice,” he added. The court imposed a 3,000 euro ($3,370) fine rather than a prison sentence. The offence carried a maximum term of four years. The 37-year-old had been allowed to return to the UK during the proceedings to attend his son’s funeral. The BBC reported that he was from Essex, near London. items.title: Bassar : L’ANID édifie les acteurs locaux et les leaders communautaires sur « l’ e-ID Togo »
items.description: Bassar, 16 oct. (ATOP) – L’Agence nationale d’identification (ANID) a organisé, les 15 et 16 octobre, un atelier de formation et de sensibilisation à l’intention des acteurs locaux et leaders communautaires des quatre communes de Bassar sur le projet d’identification biométrique « e-ID Togo ». L’objectif est d’éclairer davantage les participants sur le processus d’enregistrement biométrique afin qu’ils puissent relayer l’information en vue d’une mobilisation collective autour du projet. Cette sensibilisation est axée sur le thème l’e-ID « une identité pour tous ». Elle intervient dans le cadre de la mise en œuvre du projet d’identification unique pour une intégration régionale. Ce projet initié par le gouvernement est soutenu par la Banque mondiale (BM) à travers le programme « WURI-Togo ». Il vise à doter chaque citoyen résident au Togo, d’un Numéro d’identification unique (NIU) afin de faciliter l’accès aux services sociaux et financiers. Les spécialistes de l’ANID ont entretenu les participants sur les éléments fondamentaux du projet, le cadre juridique et institutionnel, l’organisation de l’enregistrement de masse. Ils ont expliqué aux acteurs leurs les rôles et responsabilités dans le processus d’enregistrement et sur la mise en place des Comités communaux de gestion de plaintes (CCGP). Les échanges ont également porté sur les missions des CCGP à savoir : recevoir et traiter convenablement les plaintes et réclamations, favoriser des solutions rapides, impartiales et confidentielles. Dr Atikpati Affo-Ogou, spécialiste en développement social à ANID, a fait savoir que moins de 15% de la population détienne une carte d’identité nationale. Il a invité les populations à s’impliquer activement dans ce processus. Dr Atikpati a précisé que l’établissement de la carte biométrique est sécurisée, gratuite et accessible dès l’âge de 5 ans. Le préfet de Bassar, Lt-col Asiah Hodabalo a souligné que ce projet gouvernemental permettra de faciliter l’accès aux services sociaux de base, de renforcer la protection sociale et de promouvoir l’inclusion financière. « L’adhésion et la mobilisation de toute la population repose sur vos épaules entend que relais d’information et leaders d’opinion. Votre rôle sera essentiel pour sensibiliser nos concitoyens dans chaque canton, village, et quartier pour que toute la population de Bassar soit en possession de cette carte », a-t-il indiqué. Le sénateur Djato Tassounti, les maires, les chefs traditionnels, les leaders religieux, les forces de l’ordre et de sécurité, les représentants des organisations de la société civile, des jeunes et personnes vivant en situation d’handicap ont assisté à la sensibilisation. ATOP/LK/BA

items.title: Troops kill two Lakurawa terrorists, recover four AK-47 rifles in Sokoto
items.description: By Kingsley Omonobi Troops of Operation Fansan Yamma have neutralised two suspected Lakurawa terrorists and recovered four AK-47 rifles, eight motorcycles and other items during clearance operations in Sokoto State. The operations were conducted on October 15, 2026, as part of sustained efforts to dismantle terrorist networks and restore security in the joint operations area. The Media Information Officer of Operation Fansan Yamma, Lt. Col. Aliyu Danja, disclosed this in a statement on Friday. Danja said troops of Sector 2 first made contact with the terrorists at Waria Forest, where they engaged them in a firefight, neutralising one and recovering two AK-47 rifles, two motorcycles and other items. He said the troops subsequently engaged another group of terrorists at Sarma village, neutralising one suspect and forcing the others to flee, abandoning their equipment. According to him, further exploitation of the area led to the recovery of six additional motorcycles, two AK-47 rifles, four magazines, 23 rounds of ammunition, one communication device and other items. The operation brings the total number of terrorists neutralised to two, while the recovered weapons and equipment are expected to support ongoing efforts to disrupt the activities of armed groups in the area. Danja said the successes demonstrated the troops’ sustained commitment to dismantling terrorist networks and restoring lasting peace and security across the joint operations area. He added that the Theatre Command appreciated the continued support and cooperation of members of the public. The military urged residents to remain vigilant and promptly report suspicious activities to the nearest security outpost. The post Troops kill two Lakurawa terrorists, recover four AK-47 rifles in Sokoto appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.description: The Minister of Interior, Dr Olubunmi Tunji-Ojo has described President Bola Tinubu as a visionary leader whose policies are intended to have long term and lasting positive impact. The minister said this at the closing ceremony of the Specialised Boarder Control and Immigration Management System (BCIMS) Training at the Immigration Headquarters on Friday in Abuja. Tunji-Ojo noted that Tinubu under the renewed hope agenda, was building a system that would stand the test of time and be in full effect even after he was out of office. “President Bola Tinubu has never been about the immediate, but the future. He understands that the most prosperous nations do not boil, cook, and eat their seeds, they plant them. “What this president is doing is planting the seed so that there will be abundance for the future,” he said. The minister said that Tinubu acknowledged that he would not be in office forever, but institutions would remain forever and what mattered was what would be handed down through generations. He commended the president for putting an end to backlogs of promotions, noting that no fewer than 50,000 personnel had gained new ranks and offices in the span of three years. “It has never happened before, but Tinubu did it. He also increased the volume of recruitment, where we now have no fewer that 40,000 new recruits at once. “When it comes to salary increment, Mr President has done it. In terms of hazard allowances, peculiar allowance, he also did,” he said. Tunji-Ojo also praised Tinubu for his dedication to the welfare of both active and retired personnel, highlighting the increase in pension of retired Comptroller- Generals of Immigration. “Previously, CGs had a pension of about N130,000, it was not encouraging. But what did the president do? He signed, and approved salary for life for CGs and DCGs. “This president has cared for the services more than any president in the history of Nigeria. He has given you his all. “And all he asks from us in the service is to do our jobs well and make Nigerians happy. Everything we have asked of him, he has done. This the least we can do,” he added. The post Tunji-Ojo praises Tinubu for approving lifetime pay for retired immigration chiefs appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Police debunk report of woman cutting off husband’s manhood in Taraba
items.description: By Femi Bolaji JALINGO — The Taraba State Police Command has debunked a viral social media report alleging that a 24-year-old woman, identified as Maimuna, severed her 30-year-old husband’s manhood, leading to his death in Maigoje village, Gashaka Local Government Area of the state. The command said preliminary verification by the Divisional Police Officer (DPO) of Gashaka Division did not establish that the alleged incident occurred. In a statement issued on Friday, October 16, 2026, the Police Public Relations Officer, ASP Victor Mshelizah, on behalf of the Commissioner of Police, CP Edwin Ogbeghagha, said inquiries conducted in Maigoje village, Mai Idanu Ward and neighbouring communities found no evidence to substantiate the report. According to the police, community members and local leaders contacted during the investigation also did not confirm the allegations. The statement read, “The Taraba State Police Command has noted a publication circulating on social media alleging that a woman identified as Maimuna inflicted injuries on her husband, Haruna Ishaka, resulting in his death in Maigoje Village, Mai Idanu Ward, Gashaka LGA. “In response, the Divisional Police Officer, Gashaka Division, conducted an on-the-ground verification exercise and made inquiries within the area and surrounding communities. “The exercise did not establish the occurrence of the alleged incident, and the communities contacted did not confirm the claims. “Based on the findings, the Command has no confirmed information substantiating the report as circulated. Members of the public are therefore advised not to treat the allegations as established facts.” The Commissioner of Police urged journalists, social media influencers and members of the public to exercise restraint and verify sensitive security-related reports through official law enforcement channels before publishing or sharing them. Ogbeghagha also warned against the deliberate fabrication and dissemination of unverified information capable of causing public disquiet or damaging individuals’ reputations. He said anyone found knowingly spreading false information would face appropriate legal consequences. The command reaffirmed its commitment to protecting lives and maintaining public order in Taraba State, urging residents to report genuine security concerns to the nearest police station. The post Police debunk report of woman cutting off husband’s manhood in Taraba appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Zelenski lanza un dardo a Trump al hablar de los europeos como “verdaderos líderes”
items.description: El presidente ucranio, Volodímir Zelenki, aguanta el tipo ante las crecientes críticas del estadounidense Donald Trump y no da muestras de querer templar lo ánimos. “Los ucranios tenemos dignidad”, ha lanzado este viernes en Bruselas, después de un nuevo rejonazo del magnate republicano, que ha dicho que Zelenski es “más difícil de tratar” que el presidente ruso, Vladímir Putin, y que es una “vergüenza” que Kiev haya reiniciado los ataques contra instalaciones energéticas de Rusia . Trump, a quien se le están complicando las elecciones de medio mandato de dentro de dos semanas, entre otras cosas por la subida de los precios del diésel, culpa a Zelenski de romper la supuesta “tregua energética” que él mismo anunció y que Rusia se saltó desde el minuto uno. items.title: 'I am a normal human being': Khawaja Asif brushes off online trolling over AI-generated Marilyn Monroe riddle
items.description: Defence Minister Khawaja Asif on Friday brushed off online trolls who mocked him for responding to an AI-generated riddle featuring Hollywood icon Marilyn Monroe on the social media platform X. On Tuesday, the defence minister and PML-N stalwart replied to an AI-generated image of Monroe on X, which asked users to spot the one item that did not belong in the AI-generated image from the 50s. Asif reshared the post and pointed out that Monroe was wearing a smartwatch in the image. The original post shared by the defence minister has since been deleted. Subsequently, netizens questioned the propriety of the post, while Indian media also published articles on Asif’s online activities . On Friday, Asif was asked about the post and whether he operated his X account himself during an appearance on Geo News programme ‘ Naya Pakistan ’. “Two hundred per cent I operate it myself,” he said. “I have a personal life and a normal life. I am a normal human being; there is nothing special about me,” he emphasised, adding that he had “no pretences”. “They presented a riddle asking about what was amiss with this photo, something that should not have been present in 1956. And that was the smartwatch, so I wrote ‘watch’. What is non-serious about this?” Asif stressed that though he was the defence minister, he operated his own account “for fun” and asked: “Am I not Khawaja Asif? If I am the defence minister, should I abandon my identity — whether it be good or bad?”

items.title: La Bourse de Casablanca termine presque en équilibre
items.description: La Bourse de Casablanca a terminé la séance de vendredi proche de l'équilibre, son indice principal, le MASI, cédant 0,01% à 16.997,92 points (pts). Le MASI 20, qui regroupe les 20 valeurs les plus liquides, et le MASI ESG, indice des entreprises ayant la meilleure notation ESG selon Moody's ESG Solutions, ont reculé de 0,14%, chacun, à 1.232,03 pts et 1.253,35 pts, respectivement. Pour sa part, le MASI Mid and Small Cap, reflétant la performance des petites et moyennes entreprises cotées, s'est stabilisé à 1.616,68 pts. Sur le plan sectoriel, les indices « Agroalimentaire / Production » (-1,65%), « Télécommunications » (-1,08%) et « Sociétés de placement immobilier » (-0,36%) ont accusé les plus fortes baisses. À l'inverse, les secteurs « Électricité » (+2,5%), « Ingénieries et biens d'équipement industriels » (+2,26%) et « Participation et promotion immobilières » (+1,83%) ont enregistré les plus fortes hausses. Le volume global des échanges s'est établi à plus de 117,42 millions de dirhams (MDH), réalisés principalement sur le marché central. Les échanges ont été dominés par Attijariwafa Bank, avec un volume de 14,28 MDH, devançant Sodep-Marsa Maroc (11,28 MDH) et Holcim Maroc (9,48 MDH). La capitalisation boursière a, quant à elle, atteint plus de 999,88 milliards de dirhams. Aux valeurs individuelles, Zellidja S.A. (-3,31% à 232,1 DH), S.M. Monétique (-2,27% à 476 DH), Cosumar (-2,23% à 173 DH), Minière Touissit (-1,78% à 4.027 DH) et Bank of Africa (-1,63% à 181 DH) ont accusé les plus fortes baisses. À l'opposé, Rebab Company (+5,99% à 93,8 DH), Wafa Assurance (+3,17% à 4.952 DH), Involys (+2,93% à 115,9 DH), Stroc Industrie (+2,81% à 157,3 DH) et Alliances (+2,56% à 360 DH) ont enregistré les plus fortes hausses. The post La Bourse de Casablanca termine presque en équilibre appeared first on Hespress Français - Actualités du Maroc .

Arsenal to retake team photo with Saliba after defender’s omission — Arteta
items.description: By Adegboyega Adeleye Arsenal manager Mikel Arteta has confirmed that the club will take a new team photograph featuring William Saliba after the defender was surprisingly left out of the official 2026/27 picture published this week. According to Sky Sports, Arteta said the original photo was arranged to meet commercial commitments after earlier attempts had been cancelled, and confirmed Saliba was “completely fine” about missing it, after being unavailable to attend due to a medical appointment. The omission surprised supporters, particularly because Saliba remains a key member of the squad. The 25-year-old has yet to play this season because of a back injury, but has made 184 appearances for Arsenal. “We will have another picture with the whole family,” Arteta said ahead of Arsenal’s trip to Nottingham Forest. “Hopefully we can get them all together at some point one day, and we’ll announce that as well.” The Arsenal boss said Saliba had been unable to attend and had taken the situation in good humour, despite some banter from teammates. The club plans to arrange a new photograph with the full squad. Saliba has resumed training on the grass as he continues his recovery. Arteta said the defender is progressing well and is due to have another MRI scan next week to assess the healing process. “Every sign so far has been very, very positive,” Arteta said. “It will be good to have him.” Arteta also said Martin Zubimendi could return against Forest after picking up an injury during the warm-down following the Leeds match. Piero Hincapie is expected to be out for another one or two weeks, while Christos Tzolis is making good progress from a hamstring injury sustained on international duty with Greece. The post Arsenal to retake team photo with Saliba after defender’s omission — Arteta appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Cabinet El Mansouri : entre énergie, social et administration, six femmes aux commandes
items.description: Le nouveau gouvernement dirigé par Fatima Ezzahra El Mansouri compte six femmes, sur un total de 32 membres, soit 21,9 % de l’équipe. De la direction de l’Exécutif aux portefeuilles de l’énergie, du développement social, de la formation professionnelle ou encore de la réforme de l’administration, elles se voient confier des responsabilités aux périmètres distincts. Tour d’horizon des fonctions attribuées aux femmes dans la nouvelle architecture gouvernementale. La composition du nouvel exécutif, nommé vendredi 16 octobre par le Roi Mohammed VI au Palais royal de Rabat, fait apparaître une présence féminine dans plusieurs domaines de l’action publique. Sur les sept femmes retenues, Fatima Ezzahra El Mansouri prend la tête du gouvernement, tandis que six autres accèdent à des fonctions ministérielles ou de ministre déléguée. Fatima Ezzahra El Mansouri à la tête de l’Exécutif La nomination de Fatima Ezzahra El Mansouri comme cheffe du gouvernement constitue le fait marquant de cette nouvelle équipe. À ce poste, elle est appelée à coordonner l’action des différents départements ministériels et à conduire la mise en œuvre du programme gouvernemental. Sa fonction la place au centre de l’architecture exécutive, avec la responsabilité de coordonner les priorités de la majorité et de suivre les principaux chantiers de l’action publique. Deux autres femmes prennent la direction de départements ministériels. Charafat Afailal hérite du ministère de l’Énergie, des Mines et du Développement durable, tandis que Najwa Koukouss est nommée ministre de la Famille, du Développement social et de l’Égalité. Le portefeuille confié à Charafat Afailal couvre des secteurs liés à la politique énergétique, à l’exploitation des ressources minières et aux objectifs de développement durable. Celui de Najwa Koukouss regroupe des domaines touchant aux politiques familiales, à l’inclusion sociale et à l’égalité. Ces deux nominations placent ainsi des femmes à la tête de départements aux champs d’intervention différents, l’un tourné notamment vers les ressources et les choix énergétiques, l’autre vers les politiques sociales. Quatre femmes ministres déléguées Quatre autres femmes rejoignent le gouvernement en qualité de ministres déléguées. Leurs attributions couvrent les relations institutionnelles, la formation professionnelle, l’habitat et la réforme administrative. Kouloub Faitah est chargée des Relations avec le Parlement et la Société civile. Sa mission porte sur les rapports entre le gouvernement et les institutions parlementaires, ainsi que sur les échanges avec les organisations de la société civile. Madiha Khayr se voit confier la Formation professionnelle et la Qualification. Ce portefeuille concerne notamment les parcours de formation, l’acquisition des compétences et la préparation aux besoins du marché du travail. Fatima Saadi est nommée ministre déléguée chargée de l’Habitat et de la Politique de la Ville. Ses attributions concernent des enjeux liés au logement, à l’aménagement urbain et aux politiques publiques destinées à améliorer les conditions d’habitat. Enfin, Aïcha Guellaa hérite de la Réforme de l’Administration. Sa mission porte sur un chantier qui concerne le fonctionnement des services publics, leur organisation et l’évolution des relations entre l’administration et les usagers. Ces quatre responsables exerceront leurs fonctions auprès des ministres auxquels leurs missions sont rattachées. Le périmètre exact de leurs interventions et les moyens mobilisés pour conduire les dossiers concernés permettront d’apprécier la portée de leurs responsabilités. Des responsabilités réparties entre plusieurs secteurs La répartition des sept nominations féminines dessine une présence dans des domaines variés. L’énergie et les mines, le développement social, les relations avec le Parlement, la formation professionnelle, l’habitat et la réforme administrative figurent parmi les secteurs concernés. Cette diversité permet de dépasser une lecture limitée au nombre de femmes présentes dans le gouvernement. Leurs attributions touchent à des politiques publiques qui concernent aussi bien les choix énergétiques que la formation, le logement, l’organisation des services publics ou les relations entre les institutions et la société civile. La distinction entre les fonctions doit toutefois être maintenue. Fatima Ezzahra El Mansouri dirige l’ensemble de l’Exécutif, Charafat Afailal et Najwa Koukouss prennent la tête de départements ministériels, tandis que Kouloub Faitah, Madiha Khayr, Fatima Saadi et Aïcha Guellaa sont chargées de missions déléguées. Le poids de ces nominations ne se mesure donc pas uniquement à travers les intitulés des postes. Il dépendra également des responsabilités effectivement exercées, des dossiers prioritaires qui leur seront confiés et de leur place dans les arbitrages gouvernementaux. Une représentation féminine de 21,9 % Sur les 32 membres de la nouvelle équipe, sept sont des femmes, soit 21,9 % de l’effectif. Cette proportion situe leur présence au sein de l’Exécutif, tandis que la répartition des fonctions permet d’en préciser les contours. La nomination d’une femme à la tête du gouvernement constitue un élément central de cette nouvelle architecture. Elle coexiste toutefois avec une représentation féminine minoritaire dans l’ensemble de l’équipe, où les responsabilités sont réparties entre des ministres de plein exercice et des ministres délégués. La composition du gouvernement offre ainsi un premier aperçu de la place accordée aux femmes dans la conduite des politiques publiques. La suite du mandat permettra de mesurer la portée concrète de leurs attributions, à travers les dossiers engagés, les décisions prises et les résultats obtenus dans leurs domaines respectifs. items.title: Dix ans après le démantèlement de la jungle de Calais : des migrant·e·s toujours plus vulnérables
items.description: En octobre 2025, le gouvernement français ordonnait le démantèlement de la "jungle" de Calais, bidonville installé dans le Nord de la France, face à la Manche et au Royaume-Uni, et destination finale de milliers de migrants venus d’Afrique et du Moyen-Orient. Une décennie plus tard, la population migrante n’a pas disparu mais ses conditions de vie se sont considérablement dégradées, pour les femmes et les enfants plus particulièrement, comme l’expliquent Marie-Charlotte Fabié, directrice Safe Passage International France, qui s’occupe de la réunification des familles, et Maïwenn Henriquet, référente santé de Médecins du Monde, dont le travail est présenté dans le documentaire "À la frontière des regards" de Charles-Henry Frizon.

items.title: GES pays promotion arrears to 56,003 teachers
items.description: The Ghana Education Service (GES) has confirmed that 56,003 teachers have received promotion-related salary adjustments and arrears, with outstanding cases awaiting validation and payment by the Controller and Accountant-General’s Department (CAGD). In a press release dated Friday, October 16, the GES said 49,725 teachers received their payments on Thursday, October 15, including arrears dating back to January 1, 2026. The remaining 6,278 teachers were paid in September 2026, bringing the total number of beneficiaries to 56,003. The Service said all outstanding cases had been fully processed and were awaiting the CAGD to reopen its portal for validation and payment. According to the GES, the CAGD’s system had been closed since October 7 to facilitate the processing of supplementary payments and October salaries. It said the outstanding payments would be completed once the department reopened the system. The GES expressed appreciation to stakeholders who supported the process, particularly the Ministry of Education, the Ministry of Employment and Labour Relations, teacher unions and the CAGD.

items.title: CE QU'UNE RÉFORME DE L'IMPÔT FONCIER DIT D'UN PAYS
items.description: Bien que la propriété immobilière soit à la fois visible et immobile, les recettes tirées des impôts sur la propriété en Afrique subsaharienne représentaient à peine 0,1 % du produit intérieur brut en 2021, contre 1 % en Europe et 1,4 % dans les pays de l'OCDE, selon une note du Fonds monétaire international publiée en 2024. Ce paradoxe soulève une question fondamentale : si la propriété est visible et immobile, pourquoi demeure-t-elle si difficile à taxer ? Les expériences de Freetown et du Bénin apportent des éléments de réponse, chacune sous un angle différent. Freetown : quand la méthode de valorisation redistribue la charge fiscale Avant 2018, le conseil municipal de Freetown n'avait pas réévalué son assiette foncière depuis plus de deux décennies. La méthode héritée de la période coloniale, fondée sur des critères peu différenciés, aboutissait à une sous-évaluation systématique des propriétés de forte valeur, faisant ainsi peser la charge fiscale de manière disproportionnée sur les propriétaires disposant des biens les moins valorisés. En 2018, la maire nouvellement élue, Yvonne Aki-Sawyerr, inscrit la réforme de la fiscalité foncière au cœur de son programme de transformation urbaine. Avec l'appui technique de l'International Centre for Tax and Development et de l'International Growth Centre, soutenus par des financements britanniques, la municipalité déploie un système de valorisation par points, combinant l'imagerie satellitaire, la collecte de données sur les caractéristiques observables des bâtiments et des données issues du marché locatif. En avril 2020, 95 % des propriétés de Freetown avaient été cartographiées et valorisées, portant le nombre de biens inscrits au registre municipal à plus du double. Les résultats de cette réforme illustrent quelque chose de plus fondamental qu'une simple amélioration technique. Le montant moyen d'impôt mis à la charge des propriétaires appartenant au quintile supérieur des propriétés les plus valorisées a progressé de 242 %, tandis que celui supporté par les propriétaires du quintile inférieur a diminué de 70 %. Le potentiel total de recettes a été multiplié par plus de cinq, dont 70 % devant provenir du quart supérieur des propriétés. Par ailleurs, les recettes effectivement collectées ont triplé dès la première année de mise en œuvre. Cette expérience met en évidence que la méthode de valorisation retenue pour asseoir l'impôt foncier n'est pas une décision purement technique. Elle détermine également la manière dont la charge fiscale est répartie entre les propriétaires, faisant ainsi de la réforme de la fiscalité foncière une question d'équité fiscale. Elle illustre toutefois une limite souvent sous-estimée. Selon les données disponibles, l'impôt n'est effectivement acquitté que pour environ 22 % des propriétés enregistrées, les mécanismes d'application des sanctions demeurant peu mobilisés. L'identification et la valorisation des propriétés constituent des étapes nécessaires mais insuffisantes : transformer le potentiel fiscal identifié en recettes effectivement mobilisées reste un défi distinct, qui engage la capacité de recouvrement de l'administration dans son ensemble. Le Bénin : quand l'efficacité de l'impôt dépend de la coordination institutionnelle Le cas du Bénin soulève une problématique différente, celle de l'architecture institutionnelle requise pour administrer efficacement un impôt foncier dans un cadre décentralisé. Au Bénin, la Taxe Foncière Unique est administrée par la Direction Générale des Impôts pour le compte des communes, qui en perçoivent 90 % du produit, l'État central retenant 10 % au titre des coûts d'administration. Le potentiel fiscal demeure toutefois très largement inexploité : une étude réalisée par la Direction Générale des Impôts en 2023 indiquait que seulement 6,35 % de ce potentiel était effectivement mobilisé. La Direction Générale des Impôts assure l'administration fiscale de la taxe, tandis que l'identification et l'actualisation des propriétés reposent sur des informations foncières produites et partagées entre plusieurs institutions, notamment l'Agence Nationale du Domaine et du Foncier et les communes. L'efficacité du dispositif dépend ainsi étroitement de la qualité de cette coordination interinstitutionnelle. Afin de renforcer cette articulation, une réforme de la méthode d'évaluation a été engagée en 2022, fondée sur une approche par zonage tenant compte de la localisation, du type d'habitation et de certaines caractéristiques observables des propriétés. Des conventions de partenariat ont par ailleurs été conclues entre la Direction Générale des Impôts et les autorités municipales afin d'améliorer l'identification des contribuables et l'acheminement des avis d'imposition. Dans ce même mouvement de modernisation, plus de 610 000 parcelles étaient enregistrées dans la base nationale e-Foncier Bénin en juin 2026, dans douze communes pilotes. Le cas béninois met en lumière une chaîne de responsabilités où chaque maillon conditionne le rendement de l'impôt. L'identification des propriétés, l'actualisation de l'information foncière, l'établissement de l'imposition et son recouvrement impliquent plusieurs institutions aux mandats distincts, et une défaillance à l'un de ces niveaux peut suffire à empêcher qu'une fraction significative du potentiel fiscal identifié se traduise par des recettes effectivement mobilisées. Droits fonciers coutumiers : quand la complexité des droits fonciers précède la question fiscale Au-delà de ces deux cas, une difficulté d'une autre nature traverse de nombreuses réformes foncières africaines, celle des terres régies par des droits fonciers coutumiers. Il s'agit de terres sur lesquelles les droits de possession ou d'usage sont reconnus selon les règles et pratiques d'une communauté, parfois sous l'autorité de chefs ou d'institutions traditionnelles, sans être nécessairement matérialisés par un titre foncier enregistré dans le système officiel de l'État. Des travaux publiés en 2025 par la Local Government Revenue Initiative montrent que l'extension de l'impôt foncier à ces espaces ne se heurte pas uniquement à des obstacles techniques, mais soulève des questions relatives à la légitimité des autorités compétentes pour reconnaître les droits fonciers, à la confiance des populations envers les collectivités locales chargées de lever l'impôt, et à l'acceptabilité d'une obligation fiscale envers des institutions dont les services rendus sont parfois insuffisamment perçus. Ces mêmes travaux indiquent toutefois qu'il n'est pas toujours nécessaire d'attendre l'achèvement d'un processus complet de formalisation foncière pour envisager la taxation. Dans certains contextes, il est possible de procéder à la cartographie des propriétés et à l'attribution d'identifiants fiscaux en tenant compte des droits et des autorités coutumières existants. Ce constat est important pour l'analyse, car il invite à ne pas réduire la faiblesse du rendement de l'impôt foncier en Afrique à la seule insuffisance des cadastres : la question des droits fonciers eux-mêmes constitue une dimension distincte qui précède souvent la question fiscale. L'impôt foncier, un révélateur des capacités réelles d'un système fiscal L'impôt foncier constitue un révélateur particulièrement riche de la capacité d'un État ou d'une collectivité à identifier la propriété, à en déterminer la valeur de façon équitable, à assurer la coordination entre les institutions qui en partagent la gestion, et à faire accepter la charge fiscale par les contribuables concernés. Un faible rendement de cet impôt peut trouver son origine dans différentes composantes du processus : l'identification des propriétés, leur valorisation, la coordination institutionnelle, le recouvrement ou encore l'acceptabilité de l'impôt. Freetown montre qu'une meilleure valorisation peut accroître fortement les recettes sans pour autant permettre de mobiliser l'ensemble du potentiel fiscal identifié. Le Bénin montre que même un potentiel fiscal identifié peut rester très largement inexploité lorsque la coordination entre les institutions fait défaut. Les zones relevant de droits fonciers coutumiers montrent que la question fiscale ne peut être dissociée de celle des droits fonciers. Une réforme de l'impôt foncier révèle ainsi bien davantage que la seule capacité d'un pays à tenir un cadastre : elle met au jour l'ensemble des conditions institutionnelles, juridiques et politiques sans lesquelles le potentiel fiscal d'un territoire ne peut se traduire par des ressources publiques effectives. Joëlle Traoré est docteure en droit public de l'Université Paris 1 Panthéon-Sorbonne. Elle est spécialisée en fiscalité internationale et africaine, avec une expertise en matière de flux financiers illicites, de réformes fiscales mondiales et de mobilisation des ressources nationales. Elle a collaboré avec des institutions africaines et internationales sur les questions de gouvernance fiscale en Afrique.

items.title: Grève générale des travailleurs le 21 octobre prochain : la CNES plaide pour la poursuite du dialogue
items.description: Le président de la Confédération nationale des employeurs du Sénégal (CNES) lance un appel pressant à la paix sociale et à la poursuite du dialogue face à la grève générale programmée par les travailleurs pour le 21 octobre prochain. Au Sénégal vu les urgences de développement et les ambitions du gouvernement, il urge selon la Confédération nationale des employeurs du Sénégal (CNES), de préserver la paix sociale face à la grève générale programmée par les travailleurs pour le 21 octobre prochain. « C'est uniquement par la prise en compte de ces préoccupations majeures des créateurs de richesse que la trêve sociale pourra être préservée. Cette relance est d'autant plus urgente que le climat social reste sous haute tension », souligne la CNES lors d’une conférence de presse tenue jeudi. A lire aussi : Le Pm Al Aminou Lo face au Secteur privé : « L’apurement de la dette intérieure sera conduit à son terme » Face à la menace de grève générale programmée par les travailleurs pour le 21 octobre prochain, le Président de la CNES lance un appel pressant à la paix sociale et à la poursuite du dialogue. « Pour la confédération, seules une méthode de suivi transparente et les garanties économiques apportées au secteur privé permettront de stabiliser durablement le pays et d'éviter un blocage préjudiciable à toute la nation », renseigne le texte. Grâce à l’implication directe du Premier ministre Ahmadou Al Aminou Lô, la CNES espère une rectification rapide de la trajectoire pour engager un partenariat tripartite sincère, équilibré et promoteur du développement de nos entreprises, industries et commerces. Les priorités économiques urgentes du secteur privé Au-delà, le patronat rappelle au gouvernement ses préoccupations prioritaires. Il s’agit notamment de l'apurement intégral et accéléré des créances dues aux entreprises, particulièrement dans les secteurs des Bâtiments et Travaux Publics (BTP), de l'Énergie et des Services, aujourd'hui asphyxiés. Il s’agit aussi de la relance effective de l'économie nationale à travers une démarche concertée avec le secteur privé, la formalisation concrète du dispositif d'appui destiné aux entreprises en difficultés du fait de l'État ou de ses démembrements. Mais aussi, la lutte contre la concurrence déloyale observée dans des secteurs industriel, commercial ainsi qu’au Port de Dakar qui met en péril la pérennité des entreprises, industries et commerces locaux et altère leur compétitivité. Mariama DIEME

items.title: Police debunk viral report of woman severing husband’s manhood in Taraba
items.description: By Femi Bolaji Taraba State Police Command has officially debunked a widely circulated news report alleging that a 24-year-old woman, Maimuna, cut off her 30-year-old husband’s manhood, leading to his death in Maigoje village, Gashaka Local Government Area. In a press statement issued on Friday, October 16, 2026, by the Police Public Relations Officer, ASP Victor Mshelizah, on behalf of the State Commissioner of Police, CP Edwin Ogbeghagha, the command stated that an on-the-ground investigation conducted by the Divisional Police Officer (DPO), Gashaka Division, found no evidence supporting the claim. According to the command, fact-finding missions across Maigoje village, Mai Idanu Ward, and neighbouring settlements revealed that no such incident occurred, adding that community members and local leaders refuted the allegations contained in the viral publication. The statement read: “The Taraba State Police Command has noted a publication circulating on social media alleging that a woman identified as Maimuna inflicted injuries on her husband, Haruna Ishaka, resulting in his death in Maigoje Village, Mai Idanu Ward, Gashaka LGA. “In response, the Divisional Police Officer, Gashaka Division, conducted an on-the-ground verification exercise and made inquiries within the area and surrounding communities. “The exercise did not establish the occurrence of the alleged incident, and the communities contacted did not confirm the claims. “Based on the findings, the Command has no confirmed information substantiating the report as circulated. Members of the public are therefore advised not to treat the allegations as established facts.” The Commissioner of Police, CP Edwin Ogbeghagha, urged journalists, social media influencers, and the general public to exercise restraint and rigorously verify sensitive security stories with official law enforcement channels before going to press. Ogbeghagha warned against the deliberate fabrication or dissemination of unverified reports capable of causing public disquiet or damaging individual reputations, adding that anyone found knowingly spreading false information would face appropriate legal consequences. The command reassured residents of Taraba State of its continued dedication to safeguarding lives and maintaining public order, encouraging citizens to report genuine security issues directly to the nearest police station. The post Police debunk viral report of woman severing husband’s manhood in Taraba appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Galamsey turning Ghana’s rivers into ‘chocolate milk’ – Sir Sam Jonah
items.description: The Chancellor of the University of Cape Coast, Sir Sam Jonah, has condemned the devastating impact of illegal mining on Ghana’s environment, warning that the destruction of rivers, forests and farmland makes it impossible to achieve meaningful sustainability. Speaking at the 25th anniversary conference of Methodist University, he described the pollution of water bodies through illegal mining, popularly known as galamsey, as not only an environmental crisis but also an economic, public health and moral concern. “Rivers that fed our young parents now have the colour of chocolate milk,” he said, illustrating the extent of the destruction caused by the practice. “This is not only an environmental problem. It is an economic problem. A health problem. And in the end, it is also a moral problem.” Sir Sam Jonah argued that galamsey reflects a failure of stewardship, with individuals pursuing financial gain at the expense of the environment and the welfare of future generations. He stressed that sustainability in Ghana must begin with confronting illegal mining and protecting the country’s natural resources. Africa must avoid repeating gold trade mistakes with AI Beyond environmental concerns, the business mogul warned that Africa risks repeating its historical mistakes in the gold trade as artificial intelligence (AI) reshapes the global economy. Drawing on his experience in the mining industry, where he began his career working underground, he said the continent could once again find itself supplying raw resources to others while importing finished products at a higher cost. He cautioned that Africa could become dependent on foreign AI technologies while exporting its data and paying to access tools developed elsewhere. “There is a real danger that Africa becomes only a consumer of these technologies and never a creator. That we buy the tools, export our data, pay rent on both,” he said. “We did that with gold for a century. I pray we don’t do this again.” Sir Sam Jonah urged African countries to invest in developing their own technologies and building the capacity to create solutions suited to their needs, rather than relying primarily on imported innovations. Mobile money proof of African innovation He cited mobile money as evidence that Africa has the capacity to develop successful, home-grown solutions when innovators focus on problems affecting local communities. “Mobile money didn’t come from Swiss banks. It grew here because millions of Africans had phones but no bank accounts. And somebody solved that problem. That is African innovation,” he said. He encouraged entrepreneurs, researchers and policymakers to apply the same approach to sectors such as agriculture, healthcare, logistics and finance, where locally developed technologies could address pressing challenges. He said the continent must move beyond being a market for imported solutions and become a creator of products, services and technologies that generate economic value. He also called for a shift from an economy dominated by job seekers to one that produces more entrepreneurs and employment opportunities. “A nation of job seekers cannot survive. We need a nation of job creators,” he said. Integrity must guide enterprise and sustainability Sir Sam Jonah anchored his message on the principles outlined in John Wesley’s 1744 sermon, The Use of Money : “Earn all you can, Save all you can, Give all you can.” He explained that earning should be driven by enterprise and innovation, saving should reflect sustainability, while giving should involve creating opportunities for others. However, he warned that these principles would lose their value without integrity. “Without integrity, gaining becomes greed, saving becomes hoarding, and giving becomes patronage,” he said. He further emphasised the importance of trust in leadership, business and institutional development, noting that it takes considerable time to establish but can be destroyed quickly. “Trust takes a decade to build and an afternoon to destroy,” he said. Universities urged to prioritise digital literacy and job creation The UCC Chancellor also challenged universities to prepare students for an economy increasingly shaped by digital technologies and innovation. He called for digital literacy to become compulsory for all students, irrespective of their disciplines, including nursing, accounting and theology. He also urged universities to ensure that research translates into practical solutions that benefit society, rather than remaining confined to academic publications and institutional shelves. According to him, higher education institutions should measure their success not only by the buildings they construct but also by the businesses their graduates establish and the jobs they create. “If by your 50th anniversary, your proudest report is not the buildings you built but the number of businesses and jobs your students created, then you would have lived your motto – Excellence, Morality, Service,” he said.

items.title: UG Communication HOD urges Ghanaians to reject politicians who thrive on insults
items.description: The Head of the Department of Communication at the University of Ghana, Professor Abena Animwaa Yeboah-Banin, has urged Ghanaians to reject politicians who use insults to gain popularity, warning that society’s tolerance of abusive political conduct encourages political parties to reward it with appointments and other opportunities. She said citizens could influence political behaviour by withdrawing attention from individuals who repeatedly use invectives, refusing to engage with their content on social media and demanding greater accountability from political leaders. Speaking during a Joy Prime dialogue on the topic ‘The Politics of Insults: Where Do We Draw the Line?’ at Labadi Beach on Friday, October 16, she argued that organised partisan politics appeared to reward such behaviour rather than condemn it. Prof. Yeboah-Banin said politicians were more likely to appoint individuals whose popularity could help them secure votes, suggesting that public acceptance of insults was contributing to the problem. She urged Ghanaians to recognise their collective power to influence political parties, stressing that politicians depended on the electorate and would respond if citizens made it clear that abusive conduct was unacceptable. “They will play the music as we want to dance,” she said, arguing that citizens had increasingly allowed politicians to dictate the tone of political discourse instead of using their influence to demand better standards. She called on the public to stop supporting media platforms and social media personalities who repeatedly promote insults, saying a change in audience behaviour could signal that the Ghanaian public no longer tolerated such conduct. The communication scholar also urged Parliament to hold ministerial nominees accountable for their public conduct during vetting, including considering whether their behaviour set an appropriate example for Ghanaian youth. She said lawmakers should question nominees whose conduct undermined the standards expected of people entrusted with positions of responsibility, and consider such behaviour when deciding whether to approve them. According to her, visible public opposition to controversial appointments could discourage future presidents from nominating individuals whose conduct was inconsistent with the expectations of public office. She warned that rewarding people who use insults could create the impression that verbal aggression was a viable route to political success and appointments. “For as long as it seems rewarding, young people would emulate that behaviour,” she said. Prof. Yeboah-Banin cautioned that if the trend continued, what appeared to be the conduct of a few individuals could become widespread, with young people believing that they had to adopt abusive behaviour to succeed in politics. She further traced some of the problem to university campuses, arguing that behaviours developed through student politics could carry into national politics. Drawing on her experience as a former vice-president of Akuafo Hall at the University of Ghana, she said she had later realised that some student leaders she worked with were already closely aligned with the New Patriotic Party (NPP) or the National Democratic Congress (NDC). She observed that individuals could gain recognition for their conduct in student politics because society had come to accept such behaviour, eventually creating pathways into positions of power. Prof. Yeboah-Banin said this could send the wrong message to younger people who wanted to succeed, encouraging them to imitate those they saw being rewarded. She therefore called for a collective shift in public attitudes, insisting that citizens, the media, Parliament and political parties all had a role to play in discouraging insults and promoting responsible conduct in Ghanaian politics.

items.title: UG Communication HOD warns insults in student politics could shape future leaders
items.description: The Head of the Department of Communication at the University of Ghana, Professor Abena Animwaa Yeboah-Banin, has warned that the normalisation of insults in student politics could influence the conduct of future political leaders and reinforce abusive practices in national politics. She said young people who witness individuals gaining recognition and political appointments through verbal attacks could come to regard such behaviour as a legitimate pathway to success. Speaking during a Joy Prime dialogue on the topic ‘The Politics of Insults: Where Do We Draw the Line?’ at Labadi Beach on Friday, October 16, Prof. Yeboah-Banin said political behaviours often began on university campuses, where student leaders could gain visibility and build connections with the country’s major political parties. Drawing on her experience as a former vice-president of Akuafo Hall at the University of Ghana, she said she had later realised that some of the student leaders she worked with were already aligned with the National Democratic Congress (NDC) or the New Patriotic Party (NPP). She argued that when individuals were noticed and elevated despite engaging in abusive conduct, it sent a signal to other young people that similar behaviour could help them secure political influence and appointments. “Because for as long as it seems rewarding, young people would emulate that behaviour,” she said. Prof. Yeboah-Banin cautioned that the trend could spread beyond a few individuals, creating a political culture in which young people believed they had to use insults to become successful. She said the responsibility for changing this pattern extended beyond politicians to the wider public, which she argued had become too tolerant of abusive political discourse. The communication scholar urged Ghanaians to reconsider the behaviour they reward with attention, particularly on social media and through media platforms that repeatedly feature individuals who use invectives. She said citizens could influence political parties by refusing to listen to or engage with such content, arguing that politicians depended on public support and votes. “They will play the music as we want to dance,” she said, stressing that voters had the collective power to compel political leaders to change their approach if they clearly rejected insults. Prof. Yeboah-Banin also called for greater scrutiny of ministerial nominees during parliamentary vetting, urging lawmakers to question candidates about conduct that could set a poor example for young people. She argued that Parliament’s assessment of nominees should take account of the standards expected of people appointed to positions of public responsibility. According to her, public resistance to appointments involving individuals known for abusive conduct could discourage future nominations of people whose behaviour did not reflect those standards. She maintained that changing the political culture required a collective effort from citizens, the media, Parliament and political parties to ensure that insults were not treated as a route to recognition, success or public office.

items.title: Police arrest 31-year-old man over alleged firearms possession, death threats in Kpando
items.description: The Volta North Regional Police Command has arrested a 31-year-old man, Saviour Dzadze, over alleged unlawful possession of firearms, cultivation of suspected narcotics and death threats. According to a police press release issued on Friday, October 16, the suspect was arrested on Wednesday, September 14, after he was identified by officers at the Kpando Circuit Court premises. The arrest followed a complaint lodged on September 8 by Dzodzi Kofi Kpakpamipke, who alleged that Mr Dzadze had threatened to kill him at gunpoint. A search of the suspect’s residence reportedly led to the recovery of an AK-47 assault rifle, a pump-action shotgun, a locally manufactured single-barrel gun, 10 AAA Lion cartridges and quantities of substances suspected to be Indian hemp. Police investigations have established that the suspect allegedly exchanged cultivated Indian hemp for the AK-47 rifle with an unidentified man from Togo. The statement added that the pump-action shotgun was obtained from his brother, Foster Dzadze, in Accra, while the locally manufactured single-barrel gun was inherited from his late father, Mathereous Dzadze. Mr Dzadze is in police custody assisting investigations and is expected to be arraigned before court, according to the police. The Volta North Regional Police Command has reiterated its commitment to fighting crime, adding that efforts are underway to arrest the suspect’s alleged accomplices to assist with investigations.

items.title: Basketball Africa League ;Le « Road to Bal 2027 » débute le 21 octobre prochain
items.description: Les qualifications pour la septième édition de la Basketball Africa League (Bal) débuteront le 21 octobre et s’achèveront le 22 novembre avec le tournoi Elite 16. Pendant quatre semaines, plus de vingt équipes se disputeront les places qualificatives à travers plusieurs tournois organisés dans les divisions Est et Ouest, notamment en Libye, à Brazzaville et à Lusaka. Selon un communiqué de la ligue, huit des équipes engagées avaient déjà participé à l’édition précédente. Avant l’Elite 16, les clubs devront franchir les tournois préliminaires répartis en cinq groupes. Dans la division Ouest, le groupe A se retrouvera en Libye, du 21 au 25 octobre. Al Ittihad (Libye), le Stade malien (Mali), Nadi Staouedi (Algérie), Nabaya (Guinée) et Kriol Star (Cap-Vert) s’y disputeront les deux premières places qualificatives. Le groupe B réunira Energie Bc (Bénin), l’As Douanes (Burkina Faso), Spintex Knights (Ghana), Npa Pythons (Liberia) et Red Flames (Sierra Leone). Les deux premiers de chaque groupe accéderont à l’Elite 16 de la division Ouest. Dans la division Est, le groupe C disputera son tournoi à Brazzaville, en République du Congo, du 24 au 28 octobre. L’Asb Onatra (Rd Congo), Fap (Cameroun), Espoir Basketball (Gabon) et Avenir du Rail (République du Congo) tenteront d’y décrocher l’une des deux places qualificatives. À Hoima, en Ouganda, le groupe D réunira Urunani (Burundi), Patriots Basketball Club (Soudan du Sud), Namuwongo Blazers (Ouganda), Cospn (Madagascar) et Ushundzi Basket (Comores). Le groupe E, pour sa part, jouera à Lusaka, en Zambie, du 27 au 31 octobre, avec Munali Suns (Zambie), Bravehearts (Malawi), Ferroviario da Beira (Mozambique) et Harare Kings (Zimbabwe). L’Elite 16 se déroulera ensuite en deux étapes : du 10 au 15 novembre à Abidjan, en Côte d’Ivoire, pour la division Ouest, puis du 17 au 22 novembre à Nairobi, au Kenya, pour la division Est. Les deux premières équipes de chaque division décrocheront leur billet pour la saison 2027 de la Bal. Des invitations spéciales (wild cards) pourraient également être attribuées afin de compléter le tableau des 16 équipes de l’Elite 16. Absa NDONG

items.description: La portavoz del PSOE, Montse Mínguez, ha anunciado su dimisión a través de un mensaje en redes sociales. Mínguez deja la portavocía de la formación y también sale de las listas para las próximas elecciones. La hasta ahora portavoz socialista toma la decisión después de las críticas de la oposición a los negocios inmobiliarios de su pareja. items.title: Political party head upset over not being appointed KP governor, claims Naqvi
items.description: LAHORE: Without taking any names, Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi on Friday claimed that the “head of a party” was “extremely upset” about not being appointed the governor of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa. “The head of a party is extremely upset over being denied a role in the new setup in KP and not getting the governorship,” Naqvi alleged while speaking to journalists in Lahore. He was seemingly referring to Jamiat Ulema-i-Islam-Fazl (JUI-F) chief Maulana Fazlur Rehman, who has been critical of the federal government over the imposition of governor’s rule in KP. This politician, Naqvi said, had remained “dependent on the establishment for decades to advance his political career”. “These are the same politicians who remained in politics for decades with the support of the establishment, and this politician even relied on the establishment to arrange air tickets for the members of his party,” he further alleged. He said such politicians had little justification for criticising others now, particularly after having benefitted from the same system they currently denounced. “Political differences are part of politics. But instead of using inappropriate language and making allegations, political leaders should speak on the basis of arguments and facts,” the minister said. Naqvi’s remarks come days after the Centre imposed governor’s rule and emergency in KP, citing the provincial government’s “deliberate disengagement” from the fight against terrorism. The move has drawn criticism from the opposition, including Fazl, as well as Mehmood Khan Achakzai and Raja Nasir Abbas of the Tehreek-i-Tahafuz Ayin-i-Pakistan. In the days preceding the imposition of governor’s rule in KP, political tensions between the Centre and the opposition — including the PTI which was in power in KP — had remained high since jailed former prime minister Imran Khan’s party announced a protest march to Islamabad to demand his release. Intense negotiations between the two sides a week before the imposition of governor’s rule had failed to yield any results while Fazl was cast as the man who could defuse heightening tensions between the Centre and the PTI. Both sides had held separate meetings with Fazl, reportedly for his intervention to help break the deadlock in the negotiations. And after the federal government imposed governor’s rule in KP, Fazl accused the Centre of reneging on its commitments amid his efforts for mediation. On Thursday, Fazl again censured the Centre, accusing it of depriving the provinces of their rights. Addressing a rally in Multan, he further recalled that his party had expressed reservations over the merger of tribal areas into KP after the 25th Constitutional Amendment in 2018. “We were not against the merger, but we said that it was an issue of the political future of the people of tribal areas,” he said, alleging that the people of those areas were not consulted on the merger. Raising doubts over the Centre’s reasoning behind imposing governor’s rule that there was a lack of cooperation on counterterrorism, he said the security situation in Balochistan was worse than it was in KP. He alleged governor’s rule was not imposed in Balochistan because the province’s chief minister “praises you”. “In KP, the PTI is in power. […] Where opposition is in power, you topple it. And the resources of former tribal areas, which had become part of the province, you have taken control of them by imposing emergency,” he remarked. During his interaction with journalists on Friday, Naqvi also spoke about the former tribal areas. He was critical of concerns regarding the allocation of resources to former tribal areas. “When the districts … were not getting their rightful share for years, why were these people silent?” he questioned. The minister commented that political leaders had failed to speak out for the rights of the people of the former tribal areas at the time, and stressed that the rights and resources of the people of those areas should be treated as an issue above political interests. Naqvi further said KP was facing serious security challenges , and called on political leaders to play a constructive role in restoring peace and combating terrorism. “Instead of fanning the flames and creating unrest, political leaders should play their role in restoring law and order and eliminating terrorism,” he said, maintaining that the province needed peace, stability and collective efforts rather than political confrontation. Separately, Punjab Chief Minister Maryam Nawaz railed against Fazl in a post on X. She said it was not expected of a senior politician such as him to support those who facilitate terrorism — an apparent reference to the PTI, which the Centre accuses of backing terrorism. She added it was unfortunate that he was supporting the party instead of “holding those accountable who were responsible for the ruin of KP because of their incompetence, ineptitude and corruption”. She also criticised Fazl for his remarks about the Chief of Defence Forces and Chief of Army Staff Field Marshal Asim Munir, seemingly referring to his comments during the Multan address about the centralisation of power. She concluded her statement by saying that no one but the PTI was “responsible for the end of its government in KP”.

items.title: Ejisu Assembly members renew calls for President Mahama to sack MCE
items.description: Assembly members in the Ejisu Municipality of the Ashanti Region have renewed calls for President John Dramani Mahama to remove Municipal Chief Executive (MCE) Jerryne Asante, expressing frustration over the lack of action on their grievances more than two months after a presidential committee was set up to investigate the matter. The aggrieved assembly members said they had met the committee, chaired by Ashanti Regional Minister Dr Frank Amoakohene, and presented their concerns about the MCE, but no action had been taken. They claim the delay has allowed Ms Asante to continue disregarding established procedures and undermining the municipality’s development. In July, the assembly members attempted to pass a vote of no confidence in the MCE but were denied access to the assembly auditorium. They have accused Ms Asante of misappropriating funds, disregarding assembly decisions and demonstrating inadequate knowledge of local governance, which they say has negatively affected development in Ejisu. Speaking on behalf of the aggrieved members, George Kuntu Blankson, the assembly member for Kwamo, said all 28 elected assembly members had resolved that they could no longer work with the MCE. “During our first press conference, we stated categorically that all the twenty-eight (28) elected Assembly Members had resolved that we would not be able to work with the Municipal Chief Executive in the person of Hon. Jerryne Asante. We gave an ultimatum of one week within which either she resigns, or the President replaces her with another person. “We wish to place on record that a Presidential Committee was formed, chaired by the Hon. Regional Minister, to look into our issues, and we appreciate that effort. “However, more than two months after our press conference, no action has been taken on it. This implies that both the MCE, Hon. Jerryne Asante and the President do not take the resolution of the Assembly Members seriously,” he said. The assembly members have also accused the MCE of working with some municipal officials to misuse the assembly’s resources. They cited the case of the Municipal Head of Works, Richard Omari-Safo, who they alleged issued a fake receipt to a resident applying for a building permit. According to the assembly members, Mr Omari-Safo was summoned before the Public Relations and Complaints Committee (PRCC), where he admitted wrongdoing. They further alleged that Principal Accountant Dennis Owusu Danquah, whom they described as an accomplice, had also been summoned before the committee to answer questions over his alleged role in the matter after signing the receipt. The assembly members accused Ms Asante of continuing to work closely with the two officials despite the allegations. They are demanding the immediate transfer of both Mr Omari-Safo and Mr Owusu Danquah from the Ejisu Municipality. The assembly members stressed that their opposition to the MCE was not motivated by personal animosity but by concerns about her leadership and its impact on the municipality. “We, the Assembly Members, do not have any personal hatred for Hon. Jerryne Asante. In fact, all of us have a very good personal relationship with her, and she will attest to this. “However, her selfish personal interest, low competence level and her lack of respect for the decisions and the authority of the General Assembly are what we are against. It is negatively affecting the Municipality so much, and we can’t sit and watch the assembly in total disarray. “That the authorities are being called upon to transfer the municipal Works Engineer, Mr Richard Omari Safo, and the Principal Accountant, Mr Dennis Owusu Danquah, from the Ejisu Municipality with immediate effect. We cannot continue to work with them any longer,” they said. Mr Blankson, who speaks for the aggrieved assembly members, issued what he described as a final warning to the President and the MCE, saying they would consider their next course of action if their demands were ignored. “This is the final notice that we are serving that we cannot work with the Municipal Chief Executive of the Ejisu Municipal Assembly, Hon. Jerryne. If this time round, she does not either resign, or the President continues to turn a deaf ear to our request, we will advise ourselves,” he said.

items.title: A Masterful Odyssey Into the Mind of Elizabeth Holmes
items.description: When he was in charge of Apple, Steve Jobs was notorious for projecting a “ reality distortion field .” That was the jokey way his employees described Jobs’s mix of charisma and bravado and his demanding management style—which would lead people to accept seemingly impossible deadlines, or to promise that they could fix unfixable problems. A malfunctioning version of the same phenomenon once surrounded Elizabeth Holmes, the disgraced founder of the failed medical start-up Theranos. She worshipped Jobs , imitating his style and unnerving confidence, even while presiding over an imploding enterprise. Her promises of a device that could affordably perform rapid medical tests with only a drop of blood were, at best, fantastical; once valued at $9 billion, Theranos collapsed into nothing. In 2022, Holmes was sentenced to 11 years in prison for defrauding her investors . In the new documentary You Can See Everything , the comedian and television auteur Nathan Fielder steps into Holmes’s reality-distortion field. Fielder, accompanied by his co-director, Lance Oppenheim, and a small camera crew, essentially moved into Holmes’s abode for the 34 days before she reported to federal prison. The team received fairly unfettered access to her, her two small children, and her partner, the entrepreneur Billy Evans, who professes obsessional devotion to Holmes. What Fielder was expecting to find while staying at the family’s Del Mar, California, rental is unclear, but he ends up in an odd and unsettling game of cat and mouse: He’s trying to suss out whether Holmes is a master manipulator or someone so deeply convinced of her own genius that she can’t distinguish fiction from fact. The film capturing that experience is an odyssey of human perception. Fielder knows that no matter how intimate his time with Holmes is, the minute the camera is trained on her, both he and the audience will be consumed by the question of whether she’s giving yet another performance. The movie unfolds and evolves over nearly three hours, spanning both the month ahead of Holmes’s May 2023 incarceration and the years following; throughout, Fielder pores over his interactions with not just Holmes but also the people around her, sifting for kernels of authenticity. What emerges is a transfixing portrait of a phenomenon most viewers will understand—a deep desire to empathize, even as we are horrified by what’s occurring or suspect we’re being lied to. [ Read: Manipulator vs. manipulator ] Holmes would disagree about that last part. Early on, she plainly states to Fielder that she has never told a lie, a statement so bewildering that it cracks his reliably deadpan expression. Watching him work to make sense of what she could mean by that, I thought of Jobs’s strange force of personality. Holmes has saucer-shaped, striking blue eyes, and she repeatedly meets Fielder’s squinty gaze with an unblinking stare and gauzy smile. Holmes may indeed be flatly misleading her interviewer, but she comes off as unnervingly sure that she’s being honest; she’s perhaps deceiving herself alongside the people in her orbit. Evans is a vital part of her new facade, which has morphed from the elite-businesswoman persona of her CEO days to that of a loving mother and partner. Holmes often has a child draped over her, and she seems profoundly attached to her worshipful partner. Yet at other times, Evans gives off a controlling air. He plucks a bowl from her because she’s not stirring eggs quickly enough. When Fielder’s questions probe too close to an uncomfortable topic, Evans will show up, put his hands on Holmes’s shoulders, and softly try to shut down the conversation. The claustrophobic proximity between Fielder and his subjects comes across visually: Oppenheim shoots them all with zoom lenses, holding on their faces for a discomfitingly long time as they wince, frown, and grin. Like his co-director, he’s searching for the truth by getting as physically close as he can. Given Holmes’s past, however, the task of uncovering anything feels impossible. Fielder is obviously uninterested in relitigating the details of Holmes’s case; she appears firmly assured that she did nothing wrong, and he knows there’s nothing he can do to tell her otherwise. Instead, he pokes at how she takes in the world, and how Evans is helping to feed her surreal self-image. It also becomes apparent that the pair are working on a new version of Theranos, chatting to investors and patent lawyers on the phone with abandon. When the harsh reality facing her—that she’ll soon have to leave her children behind—peeks through, her devastation seems genuine. But those moments then flit by as Holmes and Evans try to ponder a brighter future. [ Read: The comic who’s his own worst enemy ] The first half of the movie consists of captivating fly-on-the-wall footage. The second half, which Fielder and Oppenheim have begged critics not to spoil (and I do think it’s fun to experience it cold), establishes You Can See Everything as one of the best films of the year. That portion finds Fielder fixating on his brief time with Holmes and the untoward influence Evans had over it: He brings in other perspectives to consult, re-creates scenes to better understand them (something he’s wont to do, especially on his fascinating HBO show, The Rehearsal ), and, most important, reckons with his role in telling this chapter of Holmes’s life story. Fielder is smart enough to know that his celebrity presence further pierces the bubble around how we perceive ourselves and one another. But he quickly developed a sort of emotional intimacy with Holmes, even as he sought to remain objective. You Can See Everything is a bold title, an invitation from Holmes that she is unlikely to follow through on. Can Fielder see everything that’s going on in her head? Beyond that, can he be an effective audience surrogate so viewers can see what he sees? The true question of this documentary isn’t just whether Holmes—who has been a figure of societal fascination for more than a decade—is putting on another performance, but also whether that’s all we, the viewers, crave from Holmes anyway.
