items.title: Octobre Rose : Dadoh University mobilise pour le dépistage de cancers du sein et de col de l’utérus
items.description: Dans le cadre d’Octobre Rose, une campagne gratuite de sensibilisation et de dépistage a été organisée à Dadoh University, au profit de la communauté universitaire. L’initiative vise à encourager les femmes et les jeunes filles à faire des examens et dépistage de cancers du sein et de col de l’utérus afin de connaître leur état de santé, tout en promouvant l’accès à l’information sanitaire à travers les plateformes numériques du projet « C’est la v ie ! ». La communauté universitaire de Dadoh University s’est mobilisée autour de la prévention des cancers féminins. Cette activité a permis à des étudiantes et au personnel de l’établissement de bénéficier de consultations et de dépistages gratuits, notamment du cancer du sein et du col de l’utérus. Des examens liés à l’hépatite B et au VIH figuraient également parmi les services évoqués par les organisateurs. Léonard Kafando, délégué général des étudiants et point focal du projet « C’est la Vie » au Burkina Faso, cette initiative répond à un double objectif : favoriser le dépistage précoce des maladies et accroître le nombre d’abonnés aux plateformes numériques du projet Pour Léonard Kafando, délégué général des étudiants et point focal du projet « C’est la vie ! » au Burkina Faso, cette initiative répond à un double objectif : favoriser le dépistage précoce des maladies et accroître le nombre d’abonnés aux plateformes numériques du projet. « Mieux vaut prévenir que guérir », a-t-il rappelé en substance, soulignant l’importance de se faire examiner avant l’apparition de complications. Le projet « C’est la vie ! », s’appuie notamment sur les réseaux sociaux Facebook, TikTok, Instagram et YouTube pour diffuser des contenus de sensibilisation. À travers une série télévisée diffusée sur A+, ses messages abordent des questions de santé, d’engagement, de développement et de leadership des jeunes. Selon Léonard Kafando, l’inscription s’effectue gratuitement, soit par le scan d’un QR code, soit à travers un lien Linktree donnant accès aux différentes plateformes. www.cestlavie.tv Les abonnés peuvent également accéder via WhatsApp, qui s’appuie sur l’intelligence artificielle pour fournir des informations relatives à la santé, à la planification familiale et au leadership des jeunes. Les contenus s’adressent principalement aux jeunes de 15 à 24 ans, sans exclure les autres catégories d’âge. Kombelempagré Soumaya estime qu’il est important de se faire dépister, même en l’absence de symptômes. Du côté des bénéficiaires, la gratuité des services et la possibilité de détecter précocement une maladie constituent des motivations essentielles. Étudiante en sciences économiques et de gestion, Kombelempagré Soumaya, estime qu’il est important de se faire dépister, même en l’absence de symptômes. Elle invite les femmes et les hommes à accorder une attention particulière à leur santé. Adjaratou Sandrine Thiombiano, directrice du service communication et marketing de Dadoh University, a souligné que le dépistage ne doit pas être limité au mois d’octobre. Dans le même sens, Adjaratou Sandrine Thiombiano, directrice du service communication et marketing de Dadoh University, a souligné que le dépistage ne doit pas être limité au mois d’octobre. Pour elle, les femmes doivent pouvoir consulter dès qu’elles ressentent une anomalie, afin de favoriser une prise en charge précoce. Elle a également insisté sur le rôle des proches, notamment des hommes, dans l’accompagnement et le soutien des femmes. Farida Kindo et Orokia Zerbo, étudiantes de l’établissement, ont, elles aussi, salué cette initiative. Elles encouragent leurs camarades à profiter de ces consultations gratuites et à ne pas considérer le cancer du sein comme une maladie réservée aux femmes âgées. Au-delà de la campagne ponctuelle, cette mobilisation rappelle que la prévention repose sur l’information, le dépistage et la solidarité. Elle invite chacun à faire de la santé une priorité, bien au-delà d’Octobre Rose. Le lien pour plus d’information: www.cestlavie.tv Hubert BADO

items.title: Bold ambitions, fragile foundations: Is Ghana ready for the AI and Data Centre risks it is inviting?
items.description: Ghana is betting big on artificial intelligence. In April 2026, President John Dramani Mahama announced a $250 million investment to build a world-class AI Computing Centre, alongside $20 million to fund the rollout of the country’s National AI Strategy. International data centre operators — Digital Realty, Africa Data Centres, PAIX, Equinix — are staking claims in Accra. MTN Ghana has pledged $1 billion over three years to strengthen digital infrastructure, including large-scale data centres and cloud computing. The ambition is unmistakable: Ghana wants to be West Africa’s digital gateway and a continental leader in responsible AI. But ambition and readiness are not the same thing. As compute-hungry AI workloads arrive, they will stress power grids that already falter, demand cybersecurity defences that remain thin, and test regulatory frameworks still moving from paper to practice. The question is not whether Ghana should pursue this future — it is whether the country has built the foundations to manage the risks that come with it. The Policy Landscape: What Ghana Has Built Ghana’s regulatory posture on AI is, on paper, among the most advanced in sub-Saharan Africa. The National AI Strategy 2023–2033, approved by Cabinet in February 2026, rests on eight pillars: AI education and workforce development, digital infrastructure, data governance, ecosystem coordination, sectoral AI adoption, applied research, ethical safeguards, and public-sector use. The strategy proposes a Responsible AI (RAI) Office to oversee implementation and lead quarterly monitoring of the country’s AI progress. The government is also developing an Emerging Technologies Bill, expected before Parliament by the end of 2026, to create binding legislation around AI, blockchain, and other frontier technologies. Ghana’s existing regulatory architecture — the Data Protection Act (Act 843), the Cybersecurity Act of 2020, and the Electronic Transactions Act — provides a legal foundation, but none of these laws were written with generative AI, autonomous decision-making, or hyperscale data centres in mind. Minister Samuel Nartey George has framed the approach clearly: the government intends to regulate harms, not curiosity. Low-risk experimentation by students and startups will be treated differently from high-risk AI systems used in lending, healthcare, or policing. That distinction is sound — but it must be enforced, not merely stated. The Data Centre Boom: Building the Physical Layer Ghana currently hosts around five major data centre facilities, clustered near Accra’s central business district and airport city. The roster of operators is growing fast. Digital Realty is establishing its first facility in Ghana. Africa Data Centres, backed by a $300 million financing partnership with the US Development Finance Corporation (DFC), is building what it calls the largest data centre in West Africa outside Nigeria. PAIX Data Centres has upgraded its Accra facility to 1.2 megawatts. Equinix has absorbed the MDXi brand for its West African division. The country’s strategic appeal is real. Ghana ranks as one of the most politically stable nations in the region. It sits at the intersection of major subsea cable routes, with over 15 carriers operating through its landing hubs. The government offers VAT and duty exemptions for designated data centre equipment. The Ghana Internet Exchange (GIX) in Accra enables local traffic routing to reduce latency and transit costs. But the investor pitch and the operational reality diverge on one critical point: power. Industrial electricity rates in Ghana range between $0.15 and $0.22 per kilowatt-hour. More importantly, the grid was not designed for the kind of dynamic, high-density demand that AI workloads generate. A single AI training run can spike power consumption to ten times baseline usage in seconds. Traditional cloud racks draw a predictable 5 to 15 kilowatts; AI-optimised racks can pull multiples of that. Without reliable and uninterrupted power, data centre operating costs climb, and the business case for hosting sensitive workloads in Ghana weakens. The Risks Ghana Must Confront Power and energy. This is the single greatest infrastructure bottleneck. AI data centres require uninterrupted power for computing, cooling, and connectivity. Ghana’s grid, while more stable than many in the region, still experiences load management and capacity constraints. The country is exploring nuclear energy — it operates a research reactor (GHARR-1) and is considering locations for a commercial nuclear power plant — but these are long-horizon projects. In the near term, data centre developers must fund their own solar, wind, battery storage, or negotiate dedicated power purchase agreements. Without grid-first policies that prevent data centre demand from competing with households and hospitals for constrained supply, Ghana risks repeating the mistakes now being corrected in the United States, where states like Virginia and Illinois are revoking data centre tax breaks over grid strain. Water consumption. Cooling remains the hidden cost. A single one-megawatt data centre can consume up to 25.5 million litres of water annually. In a country already managing water access challenges, scaling data centre capacity without mandating water-efficient cooling technologies would be irresponsible. Brain drain and skills gap. Professor Jerry John Kponyo of KNUST has warned that without deliberate safeguards, Ghana’s AI strategy could accelerate brain drain, as the country’s best technology talent migrates abroad. The pipeline of AI-ready professionals — data scientists, machine learning engineers, cybersecurity specialists — remains thin. Only 247 public-sector personnel have been trained in AI so far. The gap between policy ambition and workforce capacity is wide. Data sovereignty. Hosting data locally is a matter of sovereignty and security. Ghana’s attraction of international data centre operators is partly about ensuring that sensitive government and corporate data does not reside on servers controlled by foreign entities in distant jurisdictions. But sovereignty requires more than physical proximity; it demands enforceable legal protections, technical competence in data governance, and operational independence from foreign vendors. Cybersecurity: The Achilles’ Heel Ghana’s cybersecurity credentials are stronger than most of its peers. The International Telecommunication Union ranks Ghana as a role model in cybersecurity, with top scores in legal, technical, organisational, and cooperative measures on the Global Cybersecurity Index. The Cybersecurity Act of 2020 provides a framework for protecting critical information infrastructure and prosecuting cybercrimes. The Cyber Security Authority (CSA), led by Dr Albert Antwi-Boasiako, coordinates national cyber defence. But the numbers tell a harder story. Ghana lost 19 million cedis (approximately $1.8 million) to cybercrime in the first nine months of 2025 alone — a 17 percent increase over the same period the year before. In 2024, several Ghanaian financial institutions faced double-extortion ransomware attacks, with attackers both encrypting and stealing sensitive data. The mass adoption of mobile payments — Ghana has over 38 million mobile subscriptions — has widened the attack surface dramatically. The proliferation of cloud services and outsourced IT has introduced supply chain vulnerabilities that the current regulatory framework does not adequately address. Small and medium-sized enterprises, which form the backbone of Ghana’s economy, lack the resources and expertise to implement robust cybersecurity strategies. The shortage of qualified cybersecurity professionals is acute. And the explosion of AI systems — many of which will be black boxes trained on opaque datasets — introduces new categories of risk: adversarial attacks on AI models, data poisoning, algorithmic bias in critical decision-making, and the weaponisation of generative AI for fraud and social engineering. Having a cybersecurity law on the books is necessary but not sufficient. Translating legal obligations into operational reality — vulnerability assessments, continuous monitoring of industrial systems, incident response readiness, and coordination between operators, regulators, and the CSA — remains the gap that matters most. Bridging the Gap: What Must Be Done Mandate energy self-sufficiency for data centres. New facilities should be required to build or fund dedicated renewable energy capacity — solar, wind, battery storage, or small modular reactors — rather than drawing from the national grid. Power purchase agreements with renewable providers should be a condition of licensing, not an afterthought. Enforce water-efficient cooling standards. As data centre capacity scales, the government should mandate liquid cooling or other water-efficient technologies and set annual water-use ceilings per megawatt of installed capacity. Invest aggressively in cybersecurity talent. Ghana cannot protect an AI-driven economy with a handful of specialists. The government should fund cybersecurity degree and certification programmes, partner with universities and innovation hubs, and offer incentives for Ghanaian cybersecurity professionals in the diaspora to return or contribute remotely. Close the gap between the Data Protection Act and AI reality. Act 843 was enacted in 2012, before generative AI existed as a practical technology. Ghana needs AI-specific data protection provisions — rules on automated decision-making, algorithmic transparency, the right to explanation, and mandatory impact assessments for high-risk AI systems deployed in financial services, healthcare, education, and law enforcement. Operationalise the Responsible AI Office. The National AI Strategy proposes this body; it must be established, funded, and given teeth — the authority to audit AI systems, investigate complaints, and enforce compliance. A strategy without an enforcement mechanism is a suggestion. Retain talent by creating opportunity at home. Brain drain is not solved by restriction but by creating compelling reasons to stay. Competitive public-sector AI roles, startup support, compute access through the new AI Computing Centre, and a clear career path in Ghana’s emerging AI ecosystem are the tools that will keep talent local. The Bottom Line Ghana’s AI and data centre ambitions are not misplaced. The country has genuine advantages — political stability, a growing digital economy, strategic geography, and policy leadership that few peers in the region can match. The $250 million AI Computing Centre, the National AI Strategy, and the Emerging Technologies Bill represent a coherent vision. But vision without execution is aspiration. The risks are not theoretical: unstable power, insufficient cooling infrastructure, a thin cybersecurity workforce, outdated data protection law, and the very real prospect of training a generation of AI professionals who leave for better-resourced markets abroad. These are not reasons to stop — they are reasons to be honest about what remains to be built. Ghana does not want to merely consume AI — it wants to shape it, regulate it, and use it as a lever for inclusive growth. That goal is achievable. But only if the country confronts its infrastructure deficits with the same boldness it brings to its policy ambitions. The world is watching. More importantly, the 33 million Ghanaians whose power, water, jobs, and data are at stake deserve nothing less. Sources: Ghana National AI Strategy – OECD AI Policy Observatory · Ghana AI Governance Framework – Regulations.ai · Ghana $250M AI Compute Investment – AU Startups · Ghana Data Centre Market – Inflect · Cybersecurity Threats in Ghana – Modern Ghana · Ghana Rising Cybercrime Costs – Data Centres Africa · AI Revolution in Accra – Modern Ghana About Author Victor Awaga is a cybersecurity, information security risk, and AI governance professional with experience in financial services. He has worked at JPMorgan Chase, Citizens Bank, and Morgan Stanley, helping organizations manage cyber risk, strengthen resilience, and address risks from emerging technologies. He holds an MBA and certifications including CISA, CISM, CRISC, Security+, and Network+.

items.title: Mahama swears in four ambassadors, tasks them to attract investment
items.description: President John Dramani Mahama has sworn in four ambassadors, urging them to prioritise investment, expand trade and create economic opportunities for Ghanaians as part of the government’s Reset Agenda. The ceremony took place at the Jubilee House on Friday, October 16, 2026. The newly sworn-in ambassadors are Nana Antwiwaa Dodoo, posted to Angola; Louis Kwame Obeng, to Qatar; Evelyn Korantemaa Ofosu-Amable, to Israel; and Jedidiah Reuben Adogla, Ghana’s Permanent Representative to the United Nations Office in Geneva, Switzerland. President Mahama urged them to use their diplomatic positions to attract investors whose interests align with Ghana’s development priorities and help local businesses access international markets. “Our missions play an important role in identifying investors whose interests align with Ghana’s development priorities, helping Ghanaian businesses enter new markets abroad, and building relationships with institutions that can support skills development, research, and technology transfer,” he said. He stressed that the success of Ghana’s economic diplomacy should be measured by the investment, jobs and other opportunities generated through international partnerships. The President also called on the ambassadors to promote local processing of Ghana’s natural resources and attract investment into productive industries to ensure the country derives greater value from its resources. He further urged them to improve consular services and protect the welfare of Ghanaians living abroad, insisting that their needs must remain a priority for Ghana’s diplomatic missions. President Mahama also highlighted Ghana’s application for partnership with the BRICS countries, explaining that the move was intended to broaden the country’s development partnerships and strengthen cooperation among developing economies. He encouraged the ambassadors to align their engagements with the government’s development priorities and use Ghana’s international relationships to deliver tangible economic benefits to the country.

items.title: Subvention « Wassa Bondo » 2026 : 320 millions FCFA accordés à 79 médias
items.description: Le ministre de la Communication, de la Culture, des Arts et du Tourisme, Pingdwendé Gilbert Ouédraogo, a présidé, ce vendredi 16 octobre 2026 à Ouagadougou, la cérémonie de remise des chèques aux médias bénéficiaires de la subvention de l’État à la presse privée au titre de l’année 2026. Cette subvention s’élève à 320 millions, répartis entre 79 médias, dont 77 entreprises de presse privées et 2 structures professionnelles. Selon la directrice générale du Fonds d’appui au sport et à la presse privée (FASP), désigné sous le nom de « Wassa Bondo », Ida Ouédraogo/Paré, pour cette année, 94 dossiers ont été réceptionnés et 79 ont finalement été retenus, après traitement par la commission indépendante de répartition, conformément à l’article 95 de l’arrêté conjoint du 9 octobre 2023. Une vue des acteurs de la presse Pour bénéficier de la subvention de l’État pour cette année 2026, les critères de sélection étaient, entre autres, la présentation de l’attestation de situation fiscale ou CNSS, de l’autorisation d’exploitation, de l’attestation de parution ou de diffusion régulière délivrée par le CSC, ainsi que du nombre requis de cartes de presse ou de journalistes professionnels par média. items.title: Hardship: Ulasi says opposition failing to win voters’ support
items.description: *Predicts Obi could defeat Tinubu in Lagos By Juliet Umeh A chieftain of the Peoples Democratic Party, PDP, Dan Ulasi, has said opposition parties are failing to turn Nigerians’ concerns over the rising cost of living into political support, despite public frustration over food prices and the cost of petrol. Ulasi also predicted that National Democratic Party’s presidential candidate, Peter Obi, could defeat President Bola Tinubu in Lagos in the 2027 general election. Speaking on Arise Television’s Morning Show, Ulasi said the opposition had not effectively made its case to Nigerians or presented clear alternatives to the policies of the All Progressives Congress, APC-led government. “There are a lot of things to exploit, but whether they’re effectively doing it is another question,” he said. Asked whether opposition parties were making the most of public dissatisfaction, Ulasi replied: “I don’t think they’re effectively doing it. I’m going to be honest to myself.” He said opposition candidates and party leaders should be holding town hall meetings across the country to explain their plans and engage voters. “You would at this point be seeing town hall meetings from zone to zone. I don’t see it happening. Nigerians are waiting for such information to feed us, and they’re not doing it.” Ulasi said the opposition was more divided than it had been ahead of the 2023 election, making it harder to challenge an incumbent president with access to state resources. “As things are on the ground, it will take some magic for anybody to stop Tinubu. The opposition is still fragmented now, worse than it was in 2023.” The PDP chieftain, who said he supports Obi, argued that the former Anambra State governor could make strong gains in several parts of the country, including Lagos, where Tinubu served as governor before becoming president. “This time around, he will beat Tinubu in Lagos State,” Ulasi said. He argued that voters in the state were questioning what they had gained from having a former Lagos governor as president. “The Lagos people, whether Yoruba or not, cannot tell you exactly that this is our son who has been president and what they have profited from it,” he said. Ulasi challenged Tinubu to hold town hall meetings across the country and explain his administration’s record to voters. “I want him to have a town hall meeting, zone to zone, telling every zone in this country what his government has done,” he said. He said Nigerians would have to protect their votes, while stressing that a fair election would be necessary for voters’ preferences to determine the outcome. “If there is a free and fair vote in this country, Peter Obi will make less than 50 per cent of votes in most states in the North,” he said. Ulasi added that the opposition’s prospects would depend not only on public dissatisfaction with the government, but also on whether its parties could organise effectively and offer voters a credible alternative. The post Hardship: Ulasi says opposition failing to win voters’ support appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Sean ‘Diddy’ Combs transferred to smaller US prison
items.description: Disgraced music producer Sean “Diddy” Combs, who was sentenced for prostitution-related crimes, has been transferred to a new US prison following media reports detailing an alleged brawl and special treatment behind bars. The 56-year-old was moved from the Fort Dix lockup in New Jersey to Allenwood Low in neighbouring Pennsylvania, a Bureau of Prisons spokeswoman told AFP on Friday. Both are low-security federal prisons for male offenders, but Allenwood Low has a population of around 1,000 compared to roughly 4,000 at Fort Dix. US media has reported that Combs was treated at a hospital for a head injury following a fight with another prisoner last weekend. And in September, NBC News reported that Combs enjoyed a relatively lavish lifestyle at Fort Dix, with access to contraband cellphones and liquor. The outlet also said Combs had men cooking and cleaning for him, as well as someone to give him Chinese-style massages. The Bureau of Prisons did not explain why Combs was transferred to the new prison. “For privacy, safety, and security reasons, we do not discuss the conditions of confinement for any individual in our custody, including reasons for transfer,” a spokeswoman said. Combs was sentenced in 2025 after a salacious trial that detailed the alleged “freak-offs” he organised: sexual marathons involving hired male escorts and his ex-girlfriend Casandra Ventura and another unidentified woman. He was acquitted by a jury of the most serious charges against him — sex trafficking and racketeering — but convicted of two counts of transporting people across state lines for prostitution. Combs is due to be released from prison in March 2028. AFP The post Sean ‘Diddy’ Combs transferred to smaller US prison appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Israeli settlers attack US photographer covering West Bank violence
items.description: Israeli settlers on Friday beat an American photojournalist working for The Washington Post while she was covering ongoing violence against Palestinian olive farmers in the occupied West Bank. Heidi Levine, a veteran photographer, was taken to hospital in Ramallah following the attack, with AFP photos showing her lying on a gurney with injuries to her leg and hand. The incident comes 10 days after settlers beat an AFP photographer covering the West Bank olive harvest , Jaafar Ashtiyeh, leaving him also requiring hospital treatment. Speaking to journalists from her hospital bed, Levine said that “more than 50” masked settlers holding sticks suddenly attacked her while she was working near the Palestinian villages of Abu Falah and Turmus Ayya in the central West Bank. “All of a sudden they jumped me and I luckily had my helmet and flak jacket on and I… kept my face to the ground to try to protect my face,” she said. “They just kept kicking me and kicking me,” she added. The Washington Post reported that Levine had been wearing a flak jacket with “Press” clearly marked on the front and back. A spokesman for the US embassy in Jerusalem said it was aware of reports of the attack, declining to comment further due to privacy laws. “We have no higher responsibility than protecting American citizens,” he said. AFP did not witness the moment of the attack, but one of the agency’s journalists in the area saw Palestinian medics tending to someone on the ground and Israeli soldiers pushing away journalists trying to approach. The Israeli military claimed troops and border police forces were deployed to the area “following a report of a violent confrontation”. “Foreign media personnel were present at the scene and a female journalist had been injured during the confrontation,” it said, adding the circumstances would be examined. “Attacks and violence against innocent civilians are grave and unacceptable acts,” the military said. The Israeli police said it had opened an investigation into incidents in Abu Falah and Turmus Ayya. “We were on our land, picking olives, and suddenly the settlers came down on us and started hitting us, throwing stones,” said Mukhllis Zuhdi, a farmer from Abu Falah. “There was even a foreign journalist whom they beat. These people have no mercy or compassion in their hearts,” he told AFP . ‘Brazen violence’ The Foreign Press Association, which represents international media in Israel and the Palestinian territories, said the settlers stole Levine’s passport, phone, wallet and equipment. “This is the latest in a long line of violent attacks by Israeli settlers against journalists and other civilians in the occupied West Bank,” it said. “Yet our repeated calls for action to confront this lawlessness have been ignored by Israeli authorities,” it added. Reporters Without Borders said it strongly condemned the attack and called on Israeli authorities to “put an end to this impunity and prosecute the perpetrators of this heinous assault”. “This brazen violence… is evidence of the impunity with which extremist Jewish settlers operate, often under the protection of Israeli armed forces,” added the advocacy group, known by its French initials RSF. Violence has flared in recent months in the West Bank, with near-daily attacks, thefts or vandalism by Israeli settlers against Palestinians. Settlers have also been seizing olive groves owned by Palestinians, who see the trees as a cultural symbol. Excluding east Jerusalem, around three million Palestinians live in the West Bank, which Israel has occupied since 1967, alongside more than 500,000 Israelis residing in settlements considered illegal under international law.

items.title: Gris Bordeaux vs Diop 2 : Jambaar Productions fixe le combat au 13 décembre 2026
items.description: Le combat entre Gris Bordeaux (Fass-Ndakaru) et Diop 2 (Yeumbeul Marin), ficelé il y a quelques semaines par Jambaar Productions, vient d’être officialisé. Ce duel dit du « Grand contre Petit », très attendu par les amateurs de lutte, aura finalement lieu le dimanche 13 décembre prochain. Gris Bordeaux et Diop 2 sont désormais fixés sur la date de leur prochaine confrontation, officialisée pour le dimanche 13 décembre. Le promoteur Mansour Bâ, patron de Jambaar Productions, a officialisé cette affiche qui opposera le 3e Tigre de Fass à l’espoir de Yeumbeul. Les deux lutteurs devront ainsi poursuivre leur préparation en vue de ce rendez-vous. L’avant-dernière phase est généralement consacrée au travail physique, avant la dernière ligne droite, axée sur les contacts et les réglages techniques. Battu par Ama Baldé le 30 juin 2024, puis par Zarco le 12 janvier 2025, Gris Bordeaux peine à retrouver le chemin de la victoire. Malgré son succès face à Siteu lors d’un duel de lutte sans frappe organisé à Paris, le samedi 2 mai dernier, le Fassois est en quête d’un véritable regain de forme en lutte avec frappe. Il n’a plus remporté de combat dans cette discipline depuis sa victoire sur Mohamed Ndao, dit Tyson, en mai 2015. De son côté, Diop 2, vainqueur de Liss Ndiago le 26 avril dernier, entend franchir un nouveau palier. Un succès contre le leader de Fass lui ouvrirait davantage les portes de la cour des Vip. Le dimanche 13 décembre sera donc une soirée de vérité pour les deux protagonistes, aux ambitions bien différentes. Abdoulaye DEMBÉLÉ

items.title: Malgré les perturbations mondiales, le FMI prévoit une croissance de 4,5% en 2026 et 2027 des pays de l’Afrique subsaharienne
items.description: Le Fonds monétaire international prévoit que l'économie de l'Afrique subsaharienne connaîtra une croissance de 4,5 % en 2026 et 2027, malgré les turbulences mondiales, la hausse des coûts de l'énergie et des importations, ainsi que la baisse de l'aide étrangère. Dans son rapport intitulé « Perspectives économiques régionales pour l’Afrique subsaharienne », publié jeudi, le FMI a maintenu ses prévisions de croissance pour les économies de la région à 4,5 % pour l’année en cours, soit le taux enregistré en 2025, et prévoit que la croissance se poursuivra au même rythme l’année prochaine. Le Fonds a revu à la hausse ses prévisions de croissance pour la région cette année de 0,2 point de pourcentage par rapport à ses estimations publiées en avril dernier, soulignant que les réformes économiques, les recettes tirées des matières premières et la capacité d’adaptation du secteur privé ont contribué à atténuer l’impact des chocs extérieurs. Les prévisions de croissance varient d’une économie à l’autre dans la région : la croissance dans les pays exportateurs de pétrole devrait atteindre 4,1 % cette année, contre 4 % l’année dernière, tandis que les autres économies riches en ressources devraient enregistrer une croissance de 3,8 %. Le Fonds a mis en garde contre les risques susceptibles d’affecter les perspectives économiques de la région, notamment la hausse des prix de l’énergie et des engrais, la baisse de l’aide étrangère, l’augmentation des coûts d’emprunt souverain, ainsi que les chocs climatiques. Il prévoit que le prix moyen du pétrole s’établira à 96 dollars le baril en 2026 et que les prix des engrais augmenteront de 26 % par rapport à l’année dernière, tandis que l’inflation dans la région devrait atteindre 4,3 % cette année, contre 3,4 % en 2025, puis 5 % en 2027. Il prévoit également une baisse supplémentaire de 12 % de l’aide bilatérale accordée à la région au cours de cette année, après une diminution d’environ un quart en 2025. Le Fonds monétaire international a appelé les gouvernements de la région à maintenir la discipline budgétaire, à orienter l'aide vers les ménages les plus vulnérables et à poursuivre les investissements productifs afin de renforcer la croissance économique à long terme.

items.title: De la guerre hybride et du sexe des anges
items.description: À télécharger Lire la note (1/2) (PDF) À télécharger Lire la note (2/2) (PDF) La légende raconte que, pendant que les troupes du sultan Mehmed II assiégeaient la ville de Constantinople, les théologiens byzantins se seraient absorbés dans un débat théologique sur le sexe des anges, négligeant la défense de la ville qui est finalement tombée le 29 mai 1453. D'où le sens donné à l’expression « discuter du sexe des anges » : se perdre en discussions futiles pendant qu'une situation urgente s'aggrave. La question de savoir si nous, Européens, sommes vraiment en guerre avec la Russie relève du même ordre d’idées. Le nier et continuer de parler de « guerre hybride » comme naguère les Byzantins du sexe des anges ne nous sera d’aucun secours. La seule vraie question est : comment s’y préparer ? items.title: Poutine : la République populaire de Lougansk est entièrement sous le contrôle des troupes russes
items.description: Reuni le 16 octobre avec les principaux responsables militaires au poste de commandement auxiliaire du groupement unifie des forces, le president russe Vladimir Poutine a fait le point sur la situation en Ukraine, en particulier a partir du rapport du chef d'etat-major general russe Valeri Guerassimov. Le president a affirme que la Republique populaire de Lougansk restait entierement sous controle russe. Il a ajoute qu'un peu plus de 10 % du territoire de la Republique populaire de Donetsk et 16,5 % de la region de Zaporojie demeuraient aux mains des forces ukrainiennes. Vladimir Poutine a mis en avant l'avancee des forces russes sur tous les axes. « L'offensive des unites et formations des forces armees se poursuit sur toute la ligne de front, et le rythme de progression s'est considerablement accelere », a-t-il declare. Selon son bilan, les forces russes ont pris le controle d'environ 6 500 km² et de 310 localites depuis le debut de l'annee. Le chef d'etat-major general a indique que, depuis le 1er septembre, 92 localites et plus de 1 800 km² etaient passes sous controle russe. Operations dans le Donbass et a Zaporojie Dans ce rapport, Valeri Guerassimov a presente les resultats des differentes unites russes. Il a notamment annonce que le groupement « Centre » avait pris Dobropolie, une ville qu'il a decrite comme l'un des principaux points de defense ukrainiens sur l'axe de Dnipropetrovsk. Selon lui, ce groupement s'est empare de 15 localites en septembre et octobre. Des combats sont en cours dans neuf autres, dont Raïskoïe et Sviatogorsk. Les forces russes poursuivent par ailleurs leur offensive en direction de Zaporojie, a-t-il signale. Vladimir Poutine a entendu le rapport du commandant du groupement « Sud » Sergueï Medvedev. Il a remercie les militaires ayant participe a la prise d'Alexeïevo-Droujkovka. Zone de securite et poursuite des frappes russes La protection des frontieres a aussi ete abordee. Vladimir Poutine a rappele qu'apres l'incursion ukrainienne dans la region de Koursk, l'armee russe avait recu pour mission de repousser l'adversaire et d'etablir une zone de securite en territoire ukrainien. Selon lui, cette tâche progresse avec succes. « Notre objectif est de garantir a l'avenir la securite absolue des territoires frontaliers de la Russie, et nous n'avons pas l'intention d'en faire un sujet de possibles negociations de paix avec l'Ukraine », a souligne le president. Un autre point de la reunion a porte sur les frappes visant les sites militaro-industriels et les infrastructures ukrainiennes. Vladimir Poutine a confirme qu'elles continueraient, les presentant comme une reponse aux attaques de Kiev contre les entreprises et les installations energetiques russes. Il a salue les resultats obtenus sur ces cibles et sur les centres logistiques ukrainiens, evoques dans le rapport de Valeri Guerassimov.

items.title: Energy Analyst Kwegyir Essel urges Atlantic Lithium to expedite compensation for Ewoyaa landowners
items.description: Energy Analyst and energy transition researcher Kwegyir Essel Isaac has called on Atlantic Lithium and its Ghanaian subsidiary, Barari DV Ghana Limited, to expedite compensation payments to eligible landowners, farmers and property owners affected by the Ewoyaa Lithium Project in the Central Region. He said the companies must prioritise the welfare of affected residents whose livelihoods have reportedly been disrupted by restrictions on land use and unresolved compensation concerns. Mr Kwegyir Essel Isaac noted that many farmers depended on their land to feed their families and generate income, warning that prolonged delays in compensation could deepen the financial difficulties facing affected households. “Their lands are frozen, their farms are inaccessible, their stomachs are empty, and their families cannot wait indefinitely for compensation,” he said. Compensation Must Follow Parliamentary Approval Following Parliament’s ratification of the mining agreement for large-scale commercial lithium mining at Ewoyaa, Mr Kwegyir Essel Isaac urged Atlantic Lithium and Barari DV Ghana Limited to work with the relevant authorities to resolve outstanding compensation claims. He maintained that Ghana’s ambition to develop its lithium industry must go hand in hand with fairness, accountability and respect for the livelihoods of communities affected by mining activities. He also called on the companies to engage with traditional authorities, landowners and other affected stakeholders to address outstanding concerns, minimise administrative delays and establish a clear timeline for payments to eligible claimants. For residents whose livelihoods depend on farming and access to their land, he said, prolonged uncertainty could undermine household incomes and economic security. He stressed that the concerns of affected residents deserved urgent attention as the project progressed. Ghana’s Lithium Wealth Must Benefit Its People Lithium is an increasingly important mineral in the global energy transition, particularly in battery manufacturing and energy storage. Ghana’s development of its lithium resources offers opportunities to attract investment, create jobs and generate revenue. However, Mr Kwegyir Essel Isaac cautioned that these potential benefits must not overshadow the welfare of communities directly affected by mining operations. He questioned the value of mineral development to farmers who could no longer cultivate their land but still had to provide for their families, as well as to landowners who remained uncertain about when they would receive legitimate compensation. He argued that responsible mineral development should not be measured solely by production figures, investment commitments or government revenue, but also by how fairly affected communities were treated and whether their livelihoods and legitimate interests were protected. Appeal to Atlantic Lithium and Government Mr Kwegyir Essel Isaac appealed directly to Atlantic Lithium, Barari DV Ghana Limited and the relevant government institutions to make the resolution of outstanding compensation claims a priority. He urged the companies to communicate transparently with affected residents, work constructively with traditional authorities and ensure that eligible landowners and farmers received the compensation due to them without unnecessary delays. He stressed that the people of Ewoyaa and surrounding communities should not be left behind as Ghana advances its critical minerals agenda. According to him, the country’s lithium ambitions should deliver shared prosperity rather than prolonged hardship for communities hosting its mineral resources. He reiterated that the development of Ghana’s lithium industry must be accompanied by fairness, accountability and respect for local livelihoods, insisting that compensation concerns required urgent attention.

items.title: Bellingham agrees new deal at Real Madrid
items.description: By Adegboyega Adeleye Real Madrid midfielder Jude Bellingham has agreed a new five-year contract that would keep him at the club until 2031, Sky Sports reports, citing Spanish newspaper AS. The reported agreement would extend the England international’s current deal, which is due to expire in 2029. The 23-year-old is also expected to receive improved terms after negotiations began towards the end of last season. According to AS, Bellingham feels at home in Madrid, feels increasingly connected to Real Madrid and life in the Spanish capital, while the club’s supporters value his commitment and influence on the pitch. Since joining from Borussia Dortmund in 2023, Bellingham has emerged as a potential leader in a Real Madrid dressing room adjusting to the departures of influential figures such as Dani Carvajal, Luka Modrić and Toni Kroos. According to the report, the club are seeking a visible figurehead capable of taking on some of the leadership those veteran players provided. He joined Real from Borussia Dortmund in 2023 in a deal that could rise to £115 million. Since then, he has helped the Spanish club win the Champions League and LaLiga. Bellingham has scored three goals and provided three assists in eight league appearances this season, with Real now managed by Jose Mourinho, who took charge in the summer. Bellingham’s importance has grown under Mourinho, whose arrival has returned the midfielder to a role he is comfortable in: operating behind Kylian Mbappé with freedom to move across the pitch. The report also highlights his work without the ball, including initiating the press and contributing defensively. His performances at the World Cup have also strengthened his standing with England. After previously having difficulties under Thomas Tuchel, he has become a key player for the national side and scored eight goals at the tournament. The reported agreement for a new deal follows Vinicius Junior’s recent contract renewal. The Brazilian forward signed a new six-year deal after attracting interest from Arsenal in the summer. The post Bellingham agrees new deal at Real Madrid appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Chants islamophobes contre l’Égypte : la FIFA sanctionne la Fédération espagnole
items.description: Plus de six mois après les chants islamophobes entendus lors du match amical entre l’Espagne et l’Égypte, disputé le 31 mars dernier à Barcelone, la Fédération espagnole de football aurait écopé d’une amende de 20 000 dollars et d’un huis clos partiel pour une prochaine rencontre organisée par la FIFA, selon Sky News. La sanction est désormais connue. La Fédération royale espagnole de football (RFEF) aurait été condamnée par la FIFA à une amende de 20 000 dollars, assortie d’un huis clos partiel lors du prochain match de la sélection espagnole organisé par l’instance internationale. Cette décision fait suite aux chants islamophobes entonnés par certains supporters espagnols lors du match amical contre l’Égypte, le 31 mars 2026, à Barcelone, conclu sur un score nul et vierge (0-0). Selon les informations rapportées par Sky News et reprises par Le Parisien, cette sanction intervient plusieurs mois après l’ouverture d’une procédure disciplinaire par la FIFA, début avril. À ce stade, aucune annonce officielle de l’instance internationale n’a toutefois été mentionnée pour confirmer ces mesures. Des chants qui avaient provoqué une vive indignation La rencontre disputée au stade Cornellà-El Prat avait été marquée par des chants à caractère islamophobe, notamment « Qui ne saute pas est musulman », entonnés par une partie des supporters présents dans les tribunes. L’incident avait suscité de nombreuses réactions en Espagne. Lamine Yamal, international espagnol de confession musulmane, avait dénoncé un « manque de respect intolérable », tandis que le Premier ministre Pedro Sánchez avait qualifié les faits d’inacceptables, regrettant que le comportement d’une minorité de supporters ait terni l’image du pays. Le milieu de terrain Pedri avait également condamné ces agissements, appelant à une mobilisation collective pour éliminer les chants racistes des stades. Le football espagnol confronté au débat sur le racisme Au-delà de la procédure disciplinaire, cet épisode avait relancé le débat sur le racisme et l’islamophobie dans les enceintes sportives espagnoles. La rencontre revêtait également une dimension symbolique, puisqu’il s’agissait de l’un des rares matchs de la sélection espagnole disputés en Catalogne depuis plus de deux décennies. La sanction rapportée rappelle la responsabilité des fédérations dans la prévention des discriminations et la lutte contre les comportements haineux dans les stades. Elle intervient dans un contexte où les instances du football sont régulièrement appelées à renforcer leurs dispositifs contre le racisme et l’intolérance. Si elle est officiellement confirmée, cette décision constituera une réponse disciplinaire aux incidents du 31 mars, sans pour autant clore le débat sur les moyens de prévenir durablement de tels débordements. The post Chants islamophobes contre l’Égypte : la FIFA sanctionne la Fédération espagnole appeared first on Hespress Français - Actualités du Maroc .

items.title: Asepex : le nouveau directeur général Amadou Diallo fixe le cap
items.description: Nommé le 10 septembre 2026 par le président de la République, le nouveau directeur général de l’Agence sénégalaise de promotion des exportations (Asepex), Amadou Diallo dit Nafaya, a été installé hier, jeudi 15 octobre. Le remplaçant de Modou Mbène Guèye a promis d’orienter sa mission vers l’entreprise, notamment les Pme-Pmi, afin de renforcer leur compétitivité. Le nouveau directeur général de l’Agence sénégalaise de promotion des exportations (Asepex), Amadou Diallo, a été installé, hier, jeudi 15 octobre, au cours d’une cérémonie. Ce fils du Fouladou, maire de la commune de Mampatim, a promis de repositionner la structure publique en misant sur le renforcement des Pme-Pmi. M. Diallo, plus connu sous le nom de Nafaya, entend inscrire son action dans la dynamique de transformation économique engagée par le gouvernement en mettant en œuvre un accompagnement ciblé, destiné à renforcer les capacités d’exportation des entreprises nationales, particulièrement celles des Pme-Pmi. Se basant sur la « Vision Sénégal 2050 », il a soutenu que l’Asepex a une responsabilité particulière dans la nouvelle stratégie engagée par les autorités. Cette responsabilité, a-t-il dit, tient en une conviction simple : la souveraineté économique ne peut être durable que si elle repose sur des entreprises fortes, compétitives, innovantes et capables de conquérir les marchés sous-régionaux, régionaux et internationaux. A lire aussi : Japon : L’Adepme accompagne 40 Pme sénégalaises à l’Expo 2025 « Notre mission sera donc orientée vers l’entreprise sénégalaise, surtout vers les Pme et les Pmi, afin de renforcer leur compétitivité et d’accroître leur capacité à conquérir durablement les marchés extérieurs », a déclaré Amadou Diallo qui succède à Modou Mbène Guèye. Il a expliqué que son objectif est de « faire passer notre économie d’une logique dans laquelle nous exportons principalement des ressources ou des produits faiblement transformés vers une logique où nous exportons davantage de produits finis, transformés et à forte valeur ajoutée ». Pour M. Diallo, l’ambition est claire : faire davantage du Sénégal un pays de production, de transformation, d’innovation et d’exportation. Il a relevé que l’entrée en vigueur de la Zone de libre-échange continentale africaine (Zlecaf) constitue une opportunité d’amélioration de la compétitivité des exportations sénégalaises, dans un contexte où la concurrence sera davantage accrue. Pour réussir sa mission, le nouveau Dg de l’Asepex compte s’appuyer, d’une part, sur le réseau des ambassades et représentations diplomatiques sénégalaises établies à l’étranger et, d’autre part, sur une collaboration étroite et dynamique avec celles des pays partenaires. Aussi, la diplomatie commerciale, estime-t-il, doit être au service de nos entreprises et de nos intérêts économiques. De même, elle doit permettre de mieux faire connaître l’offre sénégalaise, de faciliter les partenariats, d’ouvrir de nouveaux débouchés et de créer les conditions favorables au développement de nos échanges commerciaux. Amadou Diallo entend également veiller au renforcement de la collaboration avec les pouvoirs publics, le secteur privé, les banques et les établissements financiers, les organisations professionnelles, les chambres consulaires, les partenaires techniques et financiers ainsi que l’ensemble des acteurs de l’écosystème économique. À l’endroit du personnel de l’Asepex, il s’engage à promouvoir une culture de travail fondée sur l’écoute, la responsabilité, la performance, la transparence et le respect des compétences. Le président du Conseil de surveillance de l’Asepex, Alioune Diop, tout comme le représentant des travailleurs, Abdou Dieng, ont promis de travailler aux côtés du nouveau directeur général pour la réussite de sa mission. Aliou KANDÉ

items.title: Exclu de la représentation au sein de la commission de supervision du dialogue, le parti FCJ a annoncé le gel de toute relation avec la coalition des partis de la majorité
items.description: Le parti « Front de la citoyenneté et de la justice » (JAM) a annoncé le gel de toute relation avec la coalition des partis de la majorité, en signe de protestation contre ce qu’il a qualifié de décision unilatérale prise par le parti au pouvoir « Insaf » concernant la nomination des représentants de la majorité au sein de la commission de supervision du dialogue national. Dans un communiqué, le Front a précisé qu’il rejetait cette décision tant sur la forme que sur le fond, estimant qu’elle n’était pas le fruit d’une concertation ou d’un consensus entre les composantes de la majorité, et qu’elle ne garantissait pas une représentation complète des différentes orientations et entités qui composent ses partis. Le Front a affirmé que, conformément aux décisions prises par son comité permanent lors de sa dernière réunion, il ne considère pas les huit personnes désignées comme ses représentantes, en particulier au sein d’une commission chargée de superviser un dialogue censé être l’occasion de débattre des grandes questions nationales et des enjeux du développement démocratique. Le Front a également appelé les parties concernées et le président de la commission de supervision du dialogue à prendre en compte sa position, soulignant que les parties qui l’ont accusé d’entraver le dialogue lors de précédentes étapes ne peuvent, selon ses propres termes, contribuer à son organisation et à sa réussite.

items.title: Africa must produce job-creators; a nation of job seekers becomes poor– Sir Sam Jonah
items.description: Ghanaian business mogul Sir Sam Jonah has charged Africa’s young people to embrace entrepreneurship and create employment opportunities rather than depend solely on government jobs for their livelihoods. He warned that African countries would struggle to overcome poverty and unemployment if young people continued to view public-sector employment as their preferred or only route to economic security. Sir Sam Jonah made the remarks on Thursday, October 15, 2026, when he addressed the Methodist University Ghana International Conference 2026, organised to commemorate the institution’s 25th anniversary. He called for a renewed appreciation of enterprise and business creation, stressing the need to encourage young people to view entrepreneurship as a respectable and viable career option. “Make enterprise respectable again. Too many of our brightest young people still see business as something you do only if you could not get a government job. A nation of job-seekers will always be poor. We need a nation of job-creators,” he said. Sir Sam Jonah acknowledged the difficulties many young graduates face in securing employment after completing tertiary education. Government institutions have traditionally been attractive to jobseekers because of the perceived stability and benefits associated with public-sector employment. Beyond encouraging young people to create jobs, he urged African governments to do more to retain their brightest graduates by creating conditions that enable them to build successful careers and businesses in their home countries. “We educate brilliant young people, at great cost, and then offer them nothing to do. Some sit at home. Some leave. Our best export is too often our best people. A sustainable Africa is one that keeps its talent working at home, not because they have no choice, but because home offers the best opportunity,” he said.

items.title: A nation of job seekers will always be poor – Sir Sam Jonah
items.description: Renowned Ghanaian businessman Sir Sam Jonah is urging African governments and young people to emphasise entrepreneurship and job creation, warning that dependence on government employment will hinder the continent’s fight against poverty and unemployment. He said Africa needed to change the perception that securing a government job is the ultimate career success, arguing that young people should be encouraged to build businesses and create opportunities for others. Sir Sam Jonah was speaking on Thursday, October 15, 2026, at the Methodist University Ghana International Conference 2026, organised to mark the university’s 25th anniversary. “Make enterprise respectable again. Too many of our brightest young people still see business as something you do only if you could not get a government job. A nation of job-seekers will always be poor. We need a nation of job-creators,” he said. His comments come amid concerns about the difficulties many graduates face in finding employment after completing tertiary education. Government institutions have traditionally attracted job-seekers due to perceived stability and benefits of public-sector employment. However, Sir Sam Jonah believes a stronger entrepreneurial culture is needed to expand employment opportunities and support Africa’s economic development. He called for greater recognition of enterprise as a viable career path, urging stakeholders to encourage young people to pursue business ideas instead of depending solely on formal employment. The businessman also challenged African governments to create an environment that allows talented graduates to build successful careers and businesses at home instead of seeking opportunities abroad. He said the continent continues to invest significant resources in educating young people but often fails to provide enough opportunities to apply their skills. “We educate brilliant young people, at great cost, and then offer them nothing to do. Some sit at home. Some leave. Our best export is too often our best people,” he said. Sir Sam Jonah argued that Africa’s long-term sustainability would depend partly on its ability to retain skilled people by creating opportunities that make staying and working on the continent an attractive choice. “A sustainable Africa is one that keeps its talent working at home, not because they have no choice, but because home offers the best opportunity,” he added.

items.title: Nigeria had records of only 40,000 expatriates when we took over – Tunji-Ojo
items.description: By Omeiza Ajayi Minister of Interior, Olubunmi Tunji-Ojo, has disclosed that when he assumed office about three years ago, official records showed only about 40,000 expatriates working in Nigeria, a figure he said was impossible for a country of 200 million people. He spoke on Friday at the closing of a training on border control and immigration management for officers of the Nigeria Immigration Service NIS. “We got into a system where, by official records, we had maybe about 40,000 foreigners or whatever working in Nigeria. In a country of 200 million, that is not possible anywhere in the world. “And when you do not have the data of those foreigners residing in your country, then how do you manage their affairs? How do you monitor them? How do you monitor someone that you don’t even know exists?” He queried. Tunji-Ojo recalled that the ministry was then overseeing “an agency that should be technologically driven,” but “that wasn’t the case.” He said the ministry decided that “Nigeria cannot continue to be at the mercy of inefficiency.” According to him, the answer was to build what he called the Centralised Interior Management and Administration System, which is bringing the records of the correctional and fire services, and civil defence, into one portal. “Harmonisation of data, strategic handshake of data generating and processing agencies is the only way to have a single point of truth,” he said. He said the reform had ended the problem of multiple identities. “We had people then, one person with two, three different passports. But today, that is history,” he said. The minister said the NIS “of today is one of the most technologically advanced immigration services in the world.” He added that the ministry now has a 10-year technology roadmap and a data centre of “over eight petabytes,” which he described as one of the biggest in Africa, with its command and control centre running completely off-grid on solar power. Tunji-Ojo also had a warning for technology vendors. “Any vendor that is not ready to transfer knowledge to you has no place in the Ministry of Interior,” he said. Earlier, Comptroller General of the NIS, Kemi Nanna Nandap, said the Border Management Information System BMIS now holds over 15 million migration records, but “that number is not the achievement.” She told the graduating officers that technology would not replace their judgement. “An alert is not a verdict,” she said. Nandap set five standards for the officers, which she described as “non-negotiable”: accuracy, integrity, judgment, readiness and accountability. On integrity, she said: “Do not share your credentials. Do not search records out of curiosity. Never use this platform to grant favours, or to settle scores, or to facilitate improper passage. Any such abuse will be investigated and punished.” She said the programme would be judged by its results. “We will judge this programme by outcomes, not ceremonies,” Nandap said. items.title: 5 iPhones that go head-to-head with Samsung’s top phones
items.description: Apple’s iPhones and Samsung continue to compete in the premium smartphone market, offering devices with advanced cameras, powerful processors, high-quality displays and artificial intelligence features. Samsung’s Galaxy S26 series competes directly with Apple’s Pro models, while Apple’s new foldable iPhone Duo introduces another challenger to Samsung’s Galaxy Z Fold range. Here are five iPhones that go head-to-head with Samsung’s top smartphones. 1. iPhone 18 Pro Max The iPhone 18 Pro Max is Apple’s premium traditional smartphone, designed for users who want high performance, advanced photography and long battery life. Introduced in September 2026, it features Apple’s A20 Pro chip and a 48-megapixel main camera with variable aperture for greater control over photography. Apple also highlights improved battery life and sustained performance. Its main rival is the Samsung Galaxy S26 Ultra, which offers a 200-megapixel main camera, advanced zoom capabilities, a 6.9-inch display and S Pen support. Both target users who want flagship performance, although Samsung places greater emphasis on long-range zoom and productivity tools. 2. iPhone 18 Pro The iPhone 18 Pro offers many of Apple’s premium features in a smaller package than the Pro Max. It is powered by the A20 Pro chip and features a 48-megapixel main camera with variable aperture, alongside improvements to battery life, cooling and camera controls. These features make it a strong option for users who want a high-end smartphone without choosing the largest model. Its closest Samsung competitor is the Galaxy S26+, which offers a 6.7-inch display, a 120Hz refresh rate and a triple-camera system with telephoto zoom. The iPhone appeals to users who prefer Apple’s iOS ecosystem, while Samsung offers Android flexibility and Galaxy AI tools. 3. iPhone Duo Apple’s iPhone Duo marks the company’s entry into the foldable smartphone market. Unveiled in September 2026, the device opens into a larger 7.6-inch display designed for multitasking and other screen-intensive activities. It also supports Apple Pencil input. Its most direct rival is Samsung’s Galaxy Z Fold series. Samsung’s foldable phones have established themselves in the large-screen smartphone category, combining a conventional outer display with an expansive inner screen. The iPhone Duo gives Apple users a foldable option, while Samsung remains an established choice for those who want Android-based multitasking and foldable productivity features. 4. iPhone 17 Pro Max Although it is no longer Apple’s newest Pro Max model, the iPhone 17 Pro Max remains a premium alternative for buyers who do not necessarily need the latest generation. It features Apple’s A19 Pro chip and a high-end camera system, making it suitable for photography, video recording, gaming and demanding applications. Its main rival is the Samsung Galaxy S26 Ultra. Samsung offers a more versatile zoom system and an integrated S Pen, while the iPhone is a strong option for users who prefer Apple’s software ecosystem and video-recording features. 5. iPhone 17e The iPhone 17e provides a more affordable entry into Apple’s current smartphone range. It features a 6.1-inch OLED display and a single rear camera, making it less focused on advanced photography than the Pro models. Its closest Samsung alternative is the Galaxy S26 FE, which offers a larger 6.7-inch display and a triple-camera setup, including a telephoto lens. The Samsung model is better suited to users who want more camera versatility, while the iPhone 17e appeals to those who prefer iOS and Apple’s device ecosystem. items.title: Le dossier du retard dans la réalisation de l’hôpital Salmane ibn Abdel Aziz examiné lors d’une réunion au ministère de la santé
items.description: Le ministère de la Santé a organisé une réunion consacrée à l'examen des causes à l’origine du retard enregistré dans la réalisation du projet de l'hôpital universitaire du roi Salmane ben Abdelaziz à Nouakchott, à l'étude des solutions permettant de surmonter les obstacles et d'accélérer le rythme des travaux. Ont participé à cette réunion la ministre de la Santé, Naha bint Mouknass, le coordinateur de l’unité de gestion du projet, des représentants du bureau d’études et du groupe saoudien Al-Amro, ainsi que des représentants du groupe saoudien Al-Qasabi, maître d’œuvre des travaux. La réunion a porté sur l’état d’avancement des travaux du projet, en identifiant les causes des retards dans la mise en œuvre et en discutant des mesures proposées pour remédier aux difficultés rencontrées, et en examinant un plan d’action visant à rattraper le retard accumulé et à garantir l’accélération du rythme des travaux. La ministre de la Santé a réaffirmé la volonté du secteur d’apporter le soutien et les facilités nécessaires, à renforcer la coordination entre les différentes parties concernées, afin de contribuer à surmonter les obstacles et à accélérer l’achèvement du projet.

items.title: Bauxite : Fadi Wazni annonce une raffinerie d’alumine pour fin 2027 et évoque 1,2 milliard USD de recettes fiscales en 2026
items.description: La Guinée pourrait exporter près de 200 millions de tonnes de bauxite en 2026, pour des recettes fiscales estimées à 1,2 milliard de dollars, selon l’homme d’affaires Fadi Wazni. Intervenant ce vendredi 16 octobre 2026 à Conakry, lors de la deuxième table ronde de l’Observatoire guinéen de conjoncture économique (OGCE), il a également annoncé que la raffinerie d’alumine en construction par son groupe et ses partenaires devrait être opérationnelle d’ici fin 2027. Organisée dans un complexe hôtelier de la capitale, cette rencontre a réuni plusieurs acteurs de l’industrie minière, des représentants de l’administration publique et des personnalités, dont l’ancien Premier ministre Ahmed Tidiane Souaré, le ministr de l’Environnement et du Développement durable, ainsi que la ministre de l’Education nationale, de l’Alphabétisation, de l’enseignement technique et de la formation professionnelle et e. Les échanges ont notamment porté sur les enjeux de l’exploitation de la bauxite et sa contribution à la transformation structurelle de l’économie guinéenne. Prenant la parole après l’ingénieur des mines Ismaël Diakité, Fadi Wazni a choisi de mettre en exergue les acquis économiques de l’exploitation minière, tout en reconnaissant les défis auxquels le secteur reste confronté. « Nous pouvons nous féliciter déjà du développement de notre industrie minière en Guinée », a-t-il déclaré, avant de reconnaître que « tout n’est pas parfait » et que les défis demeurent nombreux. Selon lui, l’un des principaux avantages de l’exploitation de la bauxite réside dans sa capacité à mobiliser une importante main-d’œuvre et à favoriser l’émergence d’entreprises de sous-traitance. L’homme d’affaires estime que les activités directement liées à la filière pourraient représenter plusieurs centaines de milliers d’emplois, tout en précisant que des études restent nécessaires pour établir des données plus précises. Il a également insisté sur les infrastructures réalisées pour accompagner le développement du secteur, notamment les routes, les chemins de fer, les ports et les bases-vie. À ses yeux, le financement de ces équipements par les investisseurs privés constitue un avantage important pour les finances publiques. « Toutes ces infrastructures sont construites sans endettement de l’État », a-t-il soutenu, évoquant également les investissements réalisés dans le cadre du projet Simandou. Une projection de 200 millions de tonnes de bauxite en 2026 Sur le plan de la production et des exportations, Fadi Wazni a avancé une projection de 200 millions de tonnes de bauxite exportées par la Guinée en 2026. D’après lui, ce volume représenterait une multiplication par plus de dix des exportations en l’espace d’une décennie. Il estime que les recettes fiscales directes tirées de cette activité pourraient atteindre 1,2 milliard de dollars cette année, sur la base d’une contribution moyenne de six dollars par tonne. « La bauxite seule va ramener un milliard deux cents millions de dollars au Trésor public », a-t-il affirmé, précisant que cette estimation ne prend pas en compte l’impôt sur les bénéfices industriels et commerciaux ni les autres contributions fiscales des entreprises intervenant dans la filière. Il a également évoqué environ 2,5 milliards de dollars de dépenses effectuées auprès d’entreprises locales, pour illustrer les retombées économiques de l’activité minière sur le tissu entrepreneurial national. Trois raffineries d’alumine en construction Au-delà de l’extraction et de l’exportation de la bauxite brute, Fadi Wazni s’est montré optimiste quant aux perspectives de transformation locale. Selon lui, trois raffineries d’alumine sont actuellement en construction en Guinée, dont celle développée par son groupe et ses partenaires, annoncée pour fin 2027. « Nous sommes déjà à pied d’œuvre et la raffinerie que nous construisons avec les partenaires va être prête fin 2027 », a-t-il assuré. Pour l’homme d’affaires, cette évolution devrait permettre à la Guinée de renforcer sa position dans la chaîne internationale de valeur de l’aluminium, en dépassant progressivement son statut de simple fournisseur de minerai brut. Il a notamment évoqué les perspectives commerciales offertes par le marché européen, soulignant que son groupe a pris le contrôle d’unités de transformation en France. Selon lui, la production guinéenne d’alumine pourrait contribuer à diversifier les sources d’approvisionnement de l’Union européenne, notamment face à sa dépendance à certains fournisseurs asiatiques et russes. « C’est une chance incroyable pour notre pays d’avoir une situation plus confortable dans la coopération internationale », a-t-il déclaré. Cette ambition s’inscrit dans une orientation plus large de transformation locale des ressources minières, également mise en avant par les autorités guinéennes. Fadi Wazni reconnaît toutefois que le passage à la production d’aluminium représente un défi industriel plus complexe, notamment en raison des exigences techniques et énergétiques liées à cette activité. Il considère néanmoins que la transformation de la bauxite en alumine constitue déjà une avancée importante. Sous-traitance : privilégier la pédagogie plutôt que la coercition Abordant les difficultés rencontrées par les entreprises locales de sous-traitance, Fadi Wazni a plaidé pour un accompagnement progressif de leur mise en conformité avec les normes applicables. Selon lui, les insuffisances constatées, notamment en matière environnementale, doivent être corrigées par la formation, la sensibilisation et l’encadrement. « Il ne faut pas être coercitif, il faut être dans la pédagogie », a-t-il insisté. Il estime que les services de l’État et les organes de régulation ont un rôle important à jouer dans l’amélioration des pratiques des entreprises. L’homme d’affaires affirme avoir constaté, au cours des dix dernières années, une amélioration significative du niveau de professionnalisation de certaines sociétés de sous-traitance, dont plusieurs se rapprocheraient désormais des standards internationaux. Un centre de formation aux métiers de l’alumine annoncé à Boké Fadi Wazni a également annoncé l’ouverture prochaine, à Boké, d’un centre de formation destiné aux métiers de l’alumine. Dénommé CPAF, selon ses déclarations, cet établissement devrait permettre de former des ingénieurs et des techniciens de haut niveau appelés à travailler dans les raffineries. Pour lui, le développement industriel doit s’accompagner de la création de compétences nationales capables de répondre aux besoins des entreprises minières. « Quand la demande est là, nous allons former, sans contrainte », a-t-il déclaré. Il a également exprimé sa confiance dans les capacités entrepreneuriales des Guinéens, estimant que les entreprises nationales pourraient, à terme, développer des compétences leur permettant d’intervenir au-delà des frontières du pays. « Je suis absolument sûr que nous allons continuer à nous développer et que nos sous-traitants vont être bientôt compétents, pas seulement pour servir la Guinée, mais même pour servir les pays voisins », a-t-il conclu. À travers cette intervention, Fadi Wazni a défendu une lecture résolument optimiste des perspectives du secteur minier guinéen, tout en reconnaissant la nécessité de poursuivre les efforts en matière de transformation industrielle, de protection environnementale et de développement des compétences locales.

items.title: Second term: Oyebanji vows to link education with jobs; Tinubu congratulates him
items.description: By Rotimi Ojomoyela President Bola Tinubu has congratulated the Governor of Ekiti State, Biodun Oyebanji on his inauguration for second term in office, urging him to consolidate on his previous achievements to deliver more dividends for the people of the state. Tinubu, represented by the Vice President, Senator Kashim Shettima at the inauguration ceremony in Ado-Ekiti, described Oyebanji’s victory as a testament of the trust that residents have in his administration and by extension, in the All Progressives Congress (APC). He further urged the residents to come en masse on January 16, 2026 and vote for President Bola Tinubu for a second term in office, in order to enjoy more dividends of democracy. Earlier in his speech, Governor Biodun Oyebanji pledged to prioritise electricity, agriculture, skills development, job creation and infrastructure in his second term, declaring that the success of his administration would be measured by the extent to which government investments improve the lives of ordinary citizens. Oyebanji said his administration would focus on translating infrastructure projects and public spending into tangible economic benefits for households, farmers, artisans, entrepreneurs and young people. The governor acknowledged the economic pressures confronting families, particularly the rising costs of food, transportation, education and other essential needs, stressing that government policies must deliver practical relief and expand opportunities for citizens. According to him, the prosperity his administration seeks must be reflected in better livelihoods, stronger businesses, productive farms, improved public services and greater economic security for families. He explained that roads should enable farmers to transport their produce to markets before harvests are lost, while reliable electricity should support industrialisation, improve productivity and help small businesses remain operational. The governor added that schools must equip children with knowledge, confidence and functional skills, while health facilities should provide accessible medical care without forcing families to exhaust their savings. Oyebanji said his administration would ensure that public expenditure was more closely linked to the everyday needs of residents, noting that development must enable people to earn better incomes, access essential services and plan their futures with greaterl confidence. On education and youth employment, the governor said his administration would strengthen the connection between formal education, practical skills and the demands of a changing economy. He described education as a defining part of Ekiti’s heritage, recalling the sacrifices made by parents who sold farm produce, postponed personal comfort and worked hard to ensure that their children received an education. “The measure of our second term will be how much of investment we have made improve the lives of our people,” he said, emphasising that roads, electricity, schools, airports and health facilities must serve clearly defined economic and social purposes. “In this second term, we will connect education more closely to enterprise, practical skills, and the need of a changing economy”. Oyebanji also pledged to expand agricultural productivity and strengthen the value chain by promoting processing, storage, packaging, transportation and marketing. He said land remained one of the state’s major economic assets, adding that government would work to ensure that farmers derived greater benefits from their labour. According to him, agricultural development requires coordinated investments in farm clusters, processing facilities, reliable electricity, water supply, transportation and access to capital. He said the administration wanted young people to view agriculture as a viable business capable of attracting knowledge, technology, investment and innovation, rather than merely as subsistence farming. The governor noted that opportunities extended beyond cultivation to other activities that could generate employment and retain more economic value within the state. “When agriculture prospers, the benefit travels from the farm to the market, from the market to the workshop, and from the workshop to the family home”. items.title: NDC to vet 54 aspirants for Western Regional executive positions October 17
items.description: The National Democratic Congress (NDC) is set to vet 54 aspirants on Saturday, October 17, as preparations gather pace for the party’s Western Regional executive elections in November. The aspirants have submitted their nominations to contest various positions in the party’s regional leadership following an earlier online nomination process. Chairman of the Regional Elections Committee, Amos Atta, said the nomination exercise was peaceful, with all 54 aspirants recorded on the committee’s dashboard as completing the in-person filing process. He said the committee encountered no challenges during the exercise and urged all aspirants to adhere to the party’s electoral guidelines to ensure a peaceful contest. “We didn’t face any challenge here. As you witnessed, it has been peaceful, and everyone came to file in peace and left in peace. We also advised them to abide by all the guidelines because, at the end of the day, we are one family, and we will come back as a family,” he said. The position of Deputy Regional Secretary reportedly attracted the highest number of aspirants, followed by Deputy Regional Youth Organiser and Regional Chairman. Mr Atta expressed confidence in the region’s preparedness for the elections, saying: “I can confidently confirm to everyone that the Western Region is 100 percent ready for the elections for the various portfolios.” Among the aspirants is Rebecca Kwoffie, a former Women’s Commissioner of the Kwame Nkrumah University of Science and Technology (KNUST) Tertiary Education Institutions Network (TEIN) and former Deputy Birmingham Women’s Organiser of the NDC in the United Kingdom. She is contesting the position of Deputy Western Regional Secretary, citing her experience in party administration, youth mobilisation and women’s leadership as key strengths. Ms Kwoffie believes her experience in various party roles would enable her to support the Regional Secretary while strengthening collaboration with the youth and women’s wings. “If you vote for me, you vote for a three-in-one package,” she said. She explained that her experience as a Women’s Commissioner and branch executive, including her service as a branch organiser, had equipped her to contribute beyond the administrative responsibilities of the Deputy Regional Secretary. She said she would work closely with the youth and women’s organisers while supporting the Regional Secretary to improve the party’s administrative efficiency. “I’ll advocate for the youth as well; I’ll also advocate for women’s empowerment, effective administration and unity,” she added. The Regional Elections Committee has reiterated its commitment to ensuring a peaceful electoral process in November 2026. Mr Atta urged aspirants and their supporters to respect the party’s electoral rules, conduct their campaigns responsibly and preserve unity throughout the contest. The vetting exercise on Saturday is expected to determine the eligibility of aspirants seeking to contest the various executive positions in the Western Region.
